@@ -5,8 +5,515 @@
             Kris Nuttycombe <kris@nutty.land>
             Daira-Emma Hopwood <daira@jacaranda.org>
             Arya <arya@zfnd.org>
-    Status: Reserved
+    Status: Draft
     Category: Consensus
     Created: 2025-09-16
     License: MIT
     Discussions-To: <https://github.com/zcash/zips/issues/1047>
+    Pull-Request: <https://github.com/zcash/zips/pull/1473>
+
+
+# Terminology
+
+The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "SHOULD", and "MAY" in this document are to
+be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [^BCP14] when, and only when, they appear
+in all capitals.
+
+The term "full validator" in this document is to be interpreted as defined in
+the Zcash protocol specification [^protocol-blockchain].
+
+The term "network upgrade" in this document is to be interpreted as described in
+ZIP 200. [^zip-0200]
+
+The character § is used when referring to sections of the Zcash Protocol
+Specification. [^protocol]
+
+The terms "v7 transaction", "bundle", "effecting data", and "authorizing data"
+are to be interpreted as described in ZIP 248. [^zip-0248]
+
+# Abstract
+
+This ZIP describes a mechanism for keys registered at the consensus level
+to be rotated, or migrated between supported signing protocols.
+
+A tracked signing key is a public key that is held in the global chain state
+under an identifier that never changes. Each identifier has an application key,
+which authorizes the actions of the ZIP that registered it (such as disbursing
+from a fund, or issuing an asset), and a rotation key, which authorizes
+replacing either of the two.
+
+This ZIP defines a bundle for the v7 transaction format that carries key
+rotation operations. An operation states the key state that it modifies, and is
+signed by both the current rotation key and the new key.
+
+Tracked signing keys, and every rotation of them, are public.
+
+# Motivation
+
+Most Zcash funds are controlled by "off-chain" signing keys, where a user
+controls some signing key authorizing spends. The consensus rules allow the
+keyholder to rotate these keys at any time, by sending funds to a new address
+(possibly in a different wallet).
+
+In a few recent ZIPs [^zip-1016] [^zip-0227], a second category of key
+management has been defined: consensus-tracked signing keys. Whether they are
+initially defined by consensus rules in a network upgrade or registered via a
+trust-on-first-use mechanism, from that point onward the consensus rules
+enforce that a specific key is used to authorize relevant on-chain actions.
+
+There are several reasons why the ability to rotate these keys is necessary:
+
+* For multisig-controlled signing keys, it can be necessary, for operational
+  reasons or in response to governance decisions, to change the set of parties
+  with authority to act as a signer. Some multisig protocols (including FROST
+  [^frost]) support refreshing key material, changing the signing keys without
+  altering the corresponding public key, but that does not provide a rotation
+  capability because the old key material can still be used to authorize
+  actions.
+* If there is concern that a particular signing protocol could be insecure, and
+  the ZIP(s) using that protocol support an alternative signing protocol,
+  having the capability to rotate tracked signing keys to the new protocol
+  means that users can choose to do so before any insecurity in the original
+  protocol can be exploited. Defining a general mechanism to support this
+  avoids each ZIP needing to provide its own migration pathway.
+
+Funding Stream addresses are also hard-coded into consensus, but rotation of
+these addresses is outside the scope of this ZIP.
+
+Two facilities define, or are proposed to define, authorization keys in
+consensus:
+
+* The Coinholder-Controlled Fund introduced by the Community and Coinholder
+  Funding Model ZIP [^zip-1016] is administered by the Key-Holder
+  Organizations. That ZIP requires the fund to be held in a multisig that
+  resists compromise of some of the parties' keys, in which no single party's
+  non-cooperation or loss of keys can lock the funds up unrecoverably. A
+  disbursement key that is fixed by the consensus rules [^zip-0272] can meet
+  both requirements only if it can be replaced without a network upgrade. A
+  change to the set of Key-Holder Organizations has already been proposed.
+  [^draft-keyholders]
+* Each ZSA Issuer has an issuance authorizing key [^zip-0227-issuer] that it
+  uses to authorize asset issuance. The corresponding validating key identifies
+  the issuer, and is part of the identifier of every asset that the issuer
+  creates. If that key is compromised, the issuer can only finalize those
+  assets and issue new ones under a new identifier.
+
+It would be beneficial for this mechanism to support rotation of both of these
+key types, and any similar key types defined by future facilities of the Zcash
+consensus protocol.
+
+## Use cases
+
+### Small-scale single issuer (e.g. toy usage)
+
+- Each issued asset uses `ik` as both the issuance key and rotation key (per default)
+- User's backup includes `isk` (or its derivation root)
+- If both consensus and the wallet is upgraded to prefer ML-DSA, then the
+  wallet can migrate the user's assets to ML-DSA by deriving `ik_ML-DSA` (or
+  generating and backing it up), then creating a single key rotation bundle
+  that:
+    - Rotates issuer `ik`'s issuance key from `ik` to `ik_ML-DSA`
+    - Rotates issuer `ik`'s rotation key from `ik` to `ik_ML-DSA`
+
+### ZSA asset bridges
+
+- `ik` is a FROST key shared among the bridge validators
+- Rotation key is held by the bridge operator (or operators via FROST)
+- Bridge operator can change the bridge validator set by rotating `ik`
+- Two bridge operators can choose to use the same validator set `ik_C`:
+    - Bridge operator A uses `rotation_key_A` to rotate their `ik_A` issuer to
+      `ik_C` (with `ik_C`'s consent)
+    - Bridge operator B uses `rotation_key_B` to rotate their `ik_B` issuer to
+      `ik_C` (with `ik_C`'s consent)
+    - If bridge operator A decides to unmerge, they use `rotation_key_A` to
+      rotate their `ik_A` issuer to `ik_A'` (or back to `ik_A`), with the
+      consent of `ik_A'` but not `rotation_key_B` or `ik_C`
+
+### Issuer merging
+
+An issuer can choose to transfer all of their controlled assets to another issuer, by creating a single key rotation bundle that:
+- Rotates issuer `ik_A`'s issuance key from `ik_A` to `ik_B`, authorized by `rotation_key_A` and `ik_B`
+- Rotates issuer `ik_A`'s rotation key from `rotation_key_A` to `rotation_key_B`, authorized by `rotation_key_A` and `rotation_key_B`
+- Issuer B now can issue all of issuer `ik_A`'s assets, without knowledge of `ik_A` (but needs to continue to use `ik_A` as the identifier for those assets due to how `assetDigest` is defined)
+
+# Privacy Implications
+
+The mechanisms defined in this ZIP are only suitable for rotation of keys that
+are publically visible in the state of the consensus protocol.
+
+Every key rotation operation is public. It links the new key to the keys that
+it replaces, and to every action authorized under the same identifier. The fee
+paid by its transaction links the key holders to the funds that paid it, unless
+those funds are shielded.
+
+A threshold signature scheme that produces ordinary signatures, such as FROST
+[^frost], reveals neither the threshold nor which of the parties signed.
+
+# Requirements
+
+- The mechanism must support both keys that are initially hard-coded in
+  consensus rules, and keys that are "register on first use".
+- The key rotation mechanism must not impose any additional requirements
+  beyond those of the signature scheme for the public key used to verify
+  the rotation being authorized.
+- The mechanism should be able to accommodate future signing protocols.
+- Public keys that are incidentally the same but used for different purposes
+  should not accidentally be rotated together.
+- A key cannot become a tracked signing key without the consent of its holder.
+- A key rotation that was authorized on the basis of one set of keys cannot
+  take effect after any of those keys has changed.
+- Signatures by tracked signing keys can be validated without access to chain
+  state, and a full validator can track the keys with a constant number of
+  state lookups and updates per signature or key rotation.
+
+# Non-requirements
+
+- This ZIP does not address rotation of spending keys associated with user
+  addresses. If users need to rotate spending keys (for example if a wallet
+  seed is compromised), it is recommended to transfer all funds out of the
+  wallet into a new wallet, and to inform counterparties that the old addresses
+  should no longer be used.
+- If a threshold signature scheme is used, the threshold need not be
+  consensus-visible.
+- This ZIP does not provide a way to recover when a rotation key is lost, or to
+  remove a tracked signing key. Either requires a network upgrade.
+
+# Specification
+
+## Tracked signing keys
+
+A tracked signing key is a public key that is held in the global chain state,
+and that full validators use to validate signatures in any transaction that
+refers to it. These are distinct from untracked (normal) signing keys, which
+are provided by transactions themselves, and are only used within the context
+of validating that single transaction.
+
+Each tracked signing key has an associated `protocol_type`, identifying the
+signing protocol that the key is for. Tracked signing keys MUST use a protocol
+type defined in this ZIP. The encoding `TrackedKey` of a tracked signing key is
+its `protocol_type` as a single byte, followed by its public key.
+
+The following protocol types are currently valid in consensus:
+
+| `protocol_type` | Signing protocol                                                                             | Public key | Signature |
+|-----------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|-----------|
+| `0x00`          | BIP 340 [^bip-0340]                                                                          | 32 bytes   | 64 bytes  |
+| `0x01`          | RedPallas, as instantiated for Orchard spend authorization [^protocol-concretespendauthsig] | 32 bytes   | 64 bytes  |
+
+A signature over a 32-byte message is *valid for* a tracked signing key if:
+
+* for BIP 340, the `Verify` algorithm of BIP 340 succeeds for that public key,
+  message, and signature;
+* for RedPallas, the public key is the encoding of a validating key
+  $\mathsf{vk}$ of $\mathsf{SpendAuthSig^{Orchard}}$, and
+  $\mathsf{SpendAuthSig^{Orchard}.Validate_{vk}}$ returns $1$ for that message
+  and signature.
+
+Protocol types, and the key usages defined below, are allocated by the ZIP
+Editors. A ZIP that needs a new one specifies it as a modification to the
+corresponding table in this ZIP.
+
+## Key usages and key pointers
+
+Each tracked signing key has an associated `key_usage`, specifying which
+sub-protocol (within the overall Zcash protocol) it is used within, and a key
+identifier `key_id` that identifies it within that usage. The pair
+`(key_usage, key_id)` is a *key pointer*. A key pointer does not change when
+its keys are rotated.
+
+The set of defined key usages for tracked signing keys is as follows:
+
+| `key_usage` | Defining ZIP                            | `key_id`                           |
+|-------------|-----------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
+| `0x01`      | ZIP 272: Consensus accounts [^zip-0272] | The 32-byte `consensus_account_id` |
+| `0x02`      | ZIP 227: ZSA issuance [^zip-0227]       | The 33-byte `issuer`               |
+
+`key_id` is treated as an opaque byte sequence within the context of this ZIP.
+The ZIP that defines a key usage specifies:
+
+* the length of `key_id`, which is the same for every key pointer of that
+  usage;
+* how its key pointers are registered (see [Key registration]);
+* which signatures are validated against the application key;
+* the protocol types that it permits for the application key, if it does not
+  permit all of them.
+
+That ZIP SHOULD require a transaction containing a signature by an application
+key to state the key pointer and the key that the signature was made for, with
+a consensus rule that the stated key is the current application key. The
+signature can then be validated without access to chain state.
+
+## Key state
+
+The global chain state is extended with a map from key pointers to key states.
+A key state is a pair of tracked signing keys:
+
+* `application_key` is the public key used to authorize subprotocol operations,
+  such as ZSA issuance or disbursement from a consensus account;
+* `rotation_key` is the public key used to authorize rotations of both
+  `application_key` and `rotation_key`.
+
+The two MAY be the same key, and the rotation key MAY be of any protocol type.
+The encoding `KeyState` of a key state is the encoding of `application_key`
+followed by that of `rotation_key`.
+
+An entry is added to this map only by [Key registration], and is modified only
+by [Key rotation operations]. Entries are never removed.
+
+## Key registration
+
+Registering a key pointer adds an entry for it to the map of key states.
+Registration MUST NOT replace an existing entry.
+
+The ZIP that defines a key usage specifies how its key pointers are registered,
+in one or both of the following ways:
+
+* By consensus rule. The key pointer and its key state are constants of the
+  consensus rules, and the entry is added at a specified block height, before
+  any transaction of that block is processed.
+* By transaction. A bundle defined by that ZIP registers a key pointer when it
+  is processed, with a key state determined by the bundle's effecting data.
+  That ZIP MUST require the transaction to contain a signature that is valid
+  for each key of the registered key state.
+
+## Key rotation bundle
+
+This ZIP defines the key rotation bundle, a bundle type for the v7 transaction
+format. [^zip-0248] Its bundle type identifier $\mathsf{KeyRotationBundleId}$
+is to be allocated in the bundle type registry of ZIP 248
+[^zip-0248-registry], and its only variant is `bundleVariant = 0`. The bundle
+moves no value, and so has no entry in `mValuePoolDeltas`.
+
+A transaction that has an entry for the key rotation bundle in `mEffectBundles`
+MUST also have one in `mAuthBundles`.
+
+### Key rotation effecting data
+
+| Bytes  | Name            | Data Type                    | Description                                             |
+|--------|-----------------|------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|
+| varies | `nKeyRotations` | `compactSize`                | The number of key rotation operations. MUST be nonzero. |
+| varies | `vKeyRotations` | `KeyRotation[nKeyRotations]` | The key rotation operations.                            |
+
+#### KeyRotation
+
+| Bytes  | Name        | Data Type    | Description                                                                         |
+|--------|-------------|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
+| 1      | `keyUsage`  | `uint8`      | The `key_usage` of the key pointer.                                                 |
+| varies | `keyId`     | `byte[]`     | The `key_id` of the key pointer, of the length specified for `keyUsage`.            |
+| 1      | `keyRole`   | `uint8`      | The key to be replaced: `0x00` for `application_key`, or `0x01` for `rotation_key`. |
+| varies | `prevState` | `KeyState`   | The key state that this operation modifies.                                         |
+| varies | `newKey`    | `TrackedKey` | The key that replaces the one selected by `keyRole`.                                |
+
+`keyUsage` MUST be a defined key usage, `keyRole` MUST be `0x00` or `0x01`, and
+the `protocol_type` of each of the three keys MUST be a defined protocol type.
+With the protocol types defined above, a `TrackedKey` is 33 bytes and a
+`KeyState` is 66 bytes.
+
+### Key rotation authorizing data
+
+| Bytes  | Name                | Data Type                        | Description                                                                        |
+|--------|---------------------|----------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
+| varies | `vKeyRotationAuths` | `KeyRotationAuth[nKeyRotations]` | The signatures for each operation, in the same order as `vKeyRotations`.          |
+
+#### KeyRotationAuth
+
+| Bytes  | Name              | Data Type             | Description                                                                     |
+|--------|-------------------|-----------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
+| varies | `rotationAuthSig` | `TrackedKeySignature` | A signature by the `rotation_key` of `prevState`, authorizing the operation.    |
+| varies | `newKeySig`       | `TrackedKeySignature` | A signature by `newKey`, showing that its holder can sign with it and consents. |
+
+#### TrackedKeySignature
+
+| Bytes             | Name              | Data Type               | Description                                                                                        |
+|-------------------|-------------------|-------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
+| varies            | `sizeSighashInfo` | `compactSize`           | The size in bytes of `sighashInfo`.                                                                |
+| `sizeSighashInfo` | `sighashInfo`     | `byte[sizeSighashInfo]` | The sighash variant and associated information, as defined in ZIP 248.                             |
+| varies            | `signature`       | `byte[]`                | A signature, of the length specified for the `protocol_type` of the key it is to be valid for.    |
+
+Sighash variant 0 is the only variant defined for the key rotation bundle, and
+its `associatedData` is the empty byte string. Both signatures in
+`vKeyRotationAuths[i]` are over the digest defined in ZIP 248, 'Variant 0
+Signature Digest' [^zip-0248-sigdigest], with
+$\mathsf{bundleType} = \mathsf{KeyRotationBundleId}$, `bundleVariant = 0`, and
+`signature_context` set to the two-byte unsigned little-endian encoding of $i$.
+
+### Key rotation digests
+
+The `bundle_effects_digest` of the key rotation bundle is a BLAKE2b-256 hash of
+the encodings of the elements of `vKeyRotations`, concatenated in order. The
+personalization field of this hash is set to:
+
+    "ZTxIdKeyRot_Hash" (1 underscore character)
+
+The `bundle_auth_digest` of the key rotation bundle is a BLAKE2b-256 hash of
+the encodings of the elements of `vKeyRotationAuths`, concatenated in order.
+The personalization field of this hash is set to:
+
+    "ZTxAuthKeyRoHash"
+
+## Key rotation operations
+
+Full validators process the key rotation bundle of a transaction after its
+other bundles. Those bundles are therefore validated against the key states as
+they were before the transaction's own key rotations, and a key pointer
+registered by a transaction can be rotated by the same transaction.
+
+The operations of a key rotation bundle are processed in order. For the
+operation `vKeyRotations[i]`, a full validator MUST reject the transaction
+unless all of the following hold:
+
+1. The key pointer `(keyUsage, keyId)` has an entry in the map of key states,
+   and that entry is equal to `prevState`.
+2. The signature in `rotationAuthSig` is valid for the `rotation_key` of
+   `prevState`.
+3. The signature in `newKeySig` is valid for `newKey`.
+4. If `keyRole` is `0x00`, the protocol type of `newKey` is one that the key
+   usage permits for the application key.
+
+It then replaces the key selected by `keyRole` in that entry with `newKey`.
+
+## Changes to ZIP 248
+
+In the section 'v7 Transaction Bundle Type Registry' [^zip-0248-registry], add
+the following row, and remove the row for key rotation from 'Potential Future
+Bundle Types':
+
+| BundleType | BundleVariant | `mValuePoolDeltas` | `mEffectBundles` | `mAuthBundles` | Defining ZIP | Bundle kind  |
+|------------|---------------|--------------------|------------------|----------------|--------------|--------------|
+| TBD        | 0             | ❌                 | ✅               | ✅             | ZIP 270      | Key rotation |
+
+# Rationale
+
+## Rationale for the key state
+
+Key states are looked up only by key pointer, never by key, so a full validator
+needs no index from keys to the key pointers that use them and no links between
+key states. A key that is used by several key pointers is rotated in each by a
+separate operation, which keeps keys that are incidentally the same from being
+rotated together.
+
+Separate key usages enable independent rotation. For example, if a Key-Holder
+Organization accidentally uses its disbursement key to issue an asset, it can
+recover from that mistake.
+
+The rotation key is part of the key state, not a tracked signing key with a key
+pointer of its own, so that it needs no rotation key in turn.
+
+Protocol type `0x00` is BIP 340 because ZIP 227 already uses that byte for it.
+The `issuer` of ZIP 227 is therefore the `TrackedKey` encoding of an issuer's
+first issuance validating key.
+
+## Rationale for stating the previous key state
+
+An operation that named only the new key would remain valid for as long as the
+rotation key was unchanged. If a rotation key's holders signed one rotation of
+the application key and later a different one, anyone holding the first
+transaction could still have it mined after the second, replacing the key that
+the holders chose with one that they had abandoned. With `prevState`, an
+operation takes effect only on the key state that its signers saw.
+
+It also puts both of the keys that an operation's signatures are validated
+against in the transaction, so signature validation needs no chain state and
+can be batched. What depends on chain state is one comparison. A full validator
+can store the map of key states as one record per key pointer, which an
+operation checks by comparing it with `prevState`, applies by overwriting one
+of its two keys, and rolls back by writing `prevState` back, with no undo data.
+
+## Rationale for the signatures
+
+The new key signs so that a key state cannot be changed to a key that nobody
+can sign with, which would leave it unusable or unrotatable until a network
+upgrade, and so that actions such as asset issuance cannot be attributed to a
+key whose holder did not agree to it.
+
+Both signatures commit to the transaction identifier, and to the position of
+the operation in the bundle. A transaction can be mined only once: a v7
+transaction that is not a coinbase transaction spends a transparent output or
+reveals a nullifier (§ 7.1.2 'Transaction Consensus Rules'
+[^protocol-txnconsensus] as modified by ZIP 248), and a coinbase transaction
+commits to its block height. A key rotation therefore cannot be replayed, even
+if later operations restore the key state that it applied to. Until it is
+mined, it stays valid while the key state equals its `prevState`; signers bound
+this with the transaction's expiry height.
+
+## Rationale for replacing one key per operation
+
+A sequence of operations that each replace a single key is equivalent to one
+operation with optional fields, without the need to define which fields are
+present, and each operation carries exactly two signatures. It also allows the
+rotation key concept to be extended in future, for example to permit multiple
+rotation keys, without a transaction format change.
+
+Processing the key rotation bundle after a transaction's other bundles allows
+an issuer to register a key and give it a separate rotation key in a single
+transaction.
+
+## Prior art
+
+The `did:plc` method used by Bluesky [^did-plc] solves a similar problem for
+account identities. As in this ZIP, an identifier is derived from the initial
+operation and never changes, rotation keys are distinct from the keys used for
+signing, and each operation names the one that it supersedes.
+
+Unlike this ZIP, `did:plc` does not require a new key to sign. It also gives an
+identifier up to five rotation keys in order of authority, and lets a
+higher-authority key replace operations signed by a lower-authority one within
+72 hours. This ZIP does not adopt that recovery window, which would make the
+outcome of a key rotation, and of every action authorized by the new key,
+provisional for its length.
+
+# Open issues
+
+* The bundle type identifier needs to be allocated in the ZIP 248 registry.
+* ZIP 317 [^zip-0317] does not yet say how key rotation operations contribute
+  to the conventional fee.
+* ZIP 227 does not yet define its key usage: registering the key pointer of an
+  issuer by its first issuance, and stating the current issuance validating
+  key in later issuance bundles separately from `issuer`.
+
+# Deployment
+
+TBD. This ZIP can only be deployed with or after the v7 transaction format.
+[^zip-0248]
+
+# Reference implementation
+
+TBD
+
+# References
+
+[^BCP14]: [Information on BCP 14 — "RFC 2119: Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels" and "RFC 8174: Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words"](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp14)
+
+[^protocol]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, Version 2026.8.0 [NU6.3] or later](protocol/protocol.pdf)
+
+[^protocol-blockchain]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, Version 2026.8.0 [NU6.3]. Section 3.3: The Block Chain](protocol/protocol.pdf#blockchain)
+
+[^protocol-concretespendauthsig]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, Version 2026.8.0 [NU6.3]. Section 5.4.7.1: Spend Authorization Signature (Sapling and Orchard)](protocol/protocol.pdf#concretespendauthsig)
+
+[^protocol-txnconsensus]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, Version 2026.8.0 [NU6.3]. Section 7.1.2: Transaction Consensus Rules](protocol/protocol.pdf#txnconsensus)
+
+[^zip-0200]: [ZIP 200: Network Upgrade Mechanism](zip-0200.rst)
+
+[^zip-0227]: [ZIP 227: Issuance of Zcash Shielded Assets](zip-0227.rst)
+
+[^zip-0227-issuer]: [ZIP 227: Issuance of Zcash Shielded Assets — Issuer Identifier](zip-0227.rst#issuer-identifier)
+
+[^zip-0248]: [ZIP 248: Extensible Transaction Format](zip-0248.rst)
+
+[^zip-0248-registry]: [ZIP 248: Extensible Transaction Format — v7 Transaction Bundle Type Registry](zip-0248.rst#v7-transaction-bundle-type-registry)
+
+[^zip-0248-sigdigest]: [ZIP 248: Extensible Transaction Format — Variant 0 Signature Digest](zip-0248.rst#variant-0-signature-digest)
+
+[^zip-0272]: [ZIP 272: Zcash Consensus Accounts](https://github.com/zcash/zips/pull/1162)
+
+[^zip-0317]: [ZIP 317: Proportional Transfer Fee Mechanism](zip-0317.rst)

+[^zip-1016]: [ZIP 1016: Community and Coinholder Funding Model](zip-1016.md)

+[^frost]: [RFC 9591: The Flexible Round-Optimized Schnorr Threshold (FROST) Protocol for Two-Round Schnorr Signatures](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/rfc9591/)

prs.title: [ZIP 272]: Define the consensus account bundles in terms of ZIP 248 and ZIP 270
prs.author: arya2
prs.bodyExcerpt: This continues #1162: its five commits rebased onto `main`, followed by three commits that bring the draft up to date with ZIP 248 (merged since) and with the ZIP 270 specification in #1473. I am not an owner of this ZIP, so take these however is easiest: review here, or pull the commits into #1162.

[^protocol] + +The terms "Mainnet" and "Testnet" are to be interpreted as described in § 3.12 +'Mainnet and Testnet'. [^protocol-blockchain]. + +The terms below are to be interpreted as follows: + +output + +: A sink of funds within the transaction that is controlled by a payment + address. This excludes e.g. miner fees, or the ZIP 233 field. + + +# Abstract + +This ZIP introduces a system of transparent consensus accounts for receiving +newly-issued ZEC, with spending from each account being controlled by a ZIP 270 +[^zip-0270] signing key. Consensus accounts supplement (but do not replace) +shielded coinbase outputs. These accounts can be funded either by new ZEC +issuance, or (in the future) by ZSA issuance transactions for other assets. +This ZIP eliminates the coinbase maturity rule while retaining the property +that all ZEC and ZSA value must enter the shielded pool(s) before it can be +otherwise transferred (or, in the case of ZEC, deshielded.) + + +# Motivation + +The Zcash development fund lockbox currently has the characteristics of a +transparent, account-based system. Spending from the lockbox requires the +introduction of a new transaction bundle that treats the lockbox as a source of +transaction inputs, controlled by a key that may be rotated using the mechanism +specified in ZIP 270 [^zip-0270]. Instead of creating a mechanism that is +specific to the development fund lockbox, creating a general mechanism provides +several benefits to consistency and usability. + +Part of the motivation for the creation of the dev fund lockbox was that the +process of shielding tens of thousands of development fund outputs (over a +thousand outputs per day) has created excessive operational friction for +key-holder entities; in addition, transactions that spend these outputs have +significant fee costs under ZIP 317 [^zip-0317]. These disadvantages do not +uniquely effect the key holders of the development fund, however; they are felt +just as acutely by miners and Zcash Community Grants. By introducing an +account-based system, all recipients of new issuance can gain the same benefits +that are available to the keyholders of the coinholder-controlled fund +introduced in ZIP 1016 [^zip-1016]. + +In addition to eliminating hassles related to UTXO management, introducing a +transparent account mechanism makes it possible for individuals to make direct +donations to the development fund lockbox. + +While this ZIP focuses on ZEC issuance, the transaction format reserves space +for asset identifiers to allow future network upgrades to extend consensus +accounts to hold Zcash Shielded Assets (ZSAs) [^zip-0227]. Such an extension +could allow a ZSA issuer to finalize ZSA issuance into a consensus account +without immediately sending the entirety of the issuance to shielded +recipients; this would enable the creation of fixed-supply ZSA assets with +publicly-visible undistributed balance, without requiring the issuer to expose +their full viewing key that would reveal the recipients of subsequent transfers +from that finalized issuance pool. + + +# Privacy Implications + +At present, all ZEC issuance is transparent, in that mining outputs are either +sent to the lockbox, sent to a transparent address, or sent to a shielded +address but with the output verified to be decryptable with the all-zeroes OVK, +to ensure that the value of each issuance output can be verified. Alternatively, they MAY continue to use + shielded coinbase outputs. +- Preserve the existing requirement that newly-issued ZEC is always shielded at + least once. +- All funding streams defined after the activation of this ZIP must use + consensus accounts as recipients. + + +# Non-requirements + +- This does not need to define a general-purpose transparent accounts + mechanism. + + +# High-level summary + +This section and the tables below are non-normative. + +Prior to this ZIP, coinbase and non-coinbase transactions supported several +different kinds of inputs and outputs. While the address receiving a shielded coinbase output is +publicly visible, the subsequent spend of that output is not distinguishable +from other shielded spends on-chain. This provides better privacy properties +than the transparent account model, and avoids requiring privacy-conscious +miners to create a new account key for each block they mine (which would +rapidly bloat the consensus account set). + + +# Specification + +## Consensus accounts + +A consensus account is uniquely identified by a `consensus_account_id`, which +is a 32-byte value derived from the account's initial public key: + +``` +consensus_account_id = BLAKE2b-256("Zcash_ConAcctId_", protocol_type || initial_public_key) +``` + +where `protocol_type || initial_public_key` is the `TrackedKey` encoding, +defined in ZIP 270 [^zip-0270], of the key provided when the account was first +registered. + +The `consensus_account_id` remains stable across key rotations performed via +ZIP 270. + +The keys that control a consensus account are the ZIP 270 key state of the key +pointer `(0x01, consensus_account_id)`. Its `application_key` authorizes the +spending of funds from the account, and MAY be any protocol type supported by +ZIP 270. + +## Global account state + +Consensus accounts require the following additions to the global state: + +- A map, `consensus_accounts`, from `consensus_account_id` to the account's + `balance`: its current ZEC balance. + +For newly registered accounts, the `application_key` and `rotation_key` of the +account's ZIP 270 key state are both set to the initial key provided at +registration. + +As of the activation of this ZIP, consensus accounts hold only ZEC. The +transaction format reserves space for asset identifiers to allow future network +upgrades to extend consensus accounts to hold other assets. + +## Initializing an account + +There are two ways to initialize a consensus account: + +- Define it in the consensus rules. + - The `consensus_account_id`s of these accounts are "visible" to the + consensus rules, and can be used in implicit rules. +- Create a miner account by mining a block that includes an account + registration bundle with a previously-unknown key. + - The `consensus_account_id`s of these accounts are "opaque" to the + consensus rules, and their balance can only be modified by being + explicitly referenced in a transaction. + +## Account registration bundle + +This ZIP defines a new bundle type for the v7 transaction format specified in +ZIP 248 [^zip-0248]. The account registration bundle registers new consensus +accounts. + +### Account Registration Effecting Data + +| Bytes | Name | Data Type | Description | +|---------|-------------------|----------------------------------------|-------------| +| varies | `nRegistrations` | `compactSize` | The number of account registrations. | +| varies | `vRegistrations` | `AccountRegistration[nRegistrations]` | New account registrations. | + +### AccountRegistration + +| Bytes | Name | Data Type | Description | +|---------|----------------|-----------------|-------------| +| 1 | `protocolType` | `uint8` | Signing protocol type as defined in ZIP 270. | +| varies | `publicKey` | `byte[keylen]` | Public key. Length is determined by `protocolType`. | + +Upon processing an `AccountRegistration`, full validators: +1. Compute the `consensus_account_id` from `protocolType` and `publicKey` as + specified above. +2. MUST reject the transaction if an account with that `consensus_account_id` + already exists. +3. Create a new account entry in `consensus_accounts` with the computed ID and + `balance` set to zero, and register the key pointer + `(0x01, consensus_account_id)` with the provided key as both + `application_key` and `rotation_key`. + +### Account Registration Authorizing Data + +| Bytes | Name | Data Type | Description | +|---------|-----------------------|--------------------------------------|-------------| +| varies | `vRegistrationAuths` | `AccountSignature[nRegistrations]` | Authorization signatures for account registrations. | + +### AccountSignature + +| Bytes | Name | Data Type | Description | +|-------------------|-------------------|-------------------------|-------------| +| varies | `sizeSighashInfo` | `compactSize` | The size in bytes of `sighashInfo`. | +| `sizeSighashInfo` | `sighashInfo` | `byte[sizeSighashInfo]` | The sighash variant and associated information, as defined in ZIP 248. | +| varies | `signature` | `byte[siglen]` | A signature. Its length is determined by the protocol type of the key that it is validated against. | + +Sighash variant 0 is the only variant defined for the bundles in this ZIP, and +its `associatedData` is the empty byte string. The signature at index $i$ of +`vRegistrationAuths` or of `vSpendAuths` is over the digest defined in ZIP 248, +'Variant 0 Signature Digest' [^zip-0248-sigdigest], with the `bundleType` and +`bundleVariant` of the bundle that contains it, and `signature_context` set to +the two-byte unsigned little-endian encoding of $i$. + +The `vRegistrationAuths` entries correspond positionally to `vRegistrations` +entries. Each signature proves control of the corresponding private key, and +MUST verify against the `publicKey` in the corresponding `AccountRegistration`. + +### Account Registration Value Pool Delta + +The account registration bundle does not transfer value; it has no entry in +`mValuePoolDeltas`. + +### Account Registration Digests + +The `bundle_effects_digest` of the account registration bundle is a BLAKE2b-256 +hash of the encodings of the elements of `vRegistrations`, concatenated in +order, with the personalization field set to `"ZTxIdAcctRegHash"`. + +Its `bundle_auth_digest` is a BLAKE2b-256 hash of the encodings of the elements +of `vRegistrationAuths`, concatenated in order, with the personalization field +set to `"ZTxAuthAcRegHash"`. + +### Account Registration Consensus Rules + +A transaction that has an entry for the account registration bundle in +`mEffectBundles` MUST also have one in `mAuthBundles`. + +In a coinbase transaction, if an account registration bundle is present, a +consensus account output bundle MUST also be present, and for each registered +account there MUST be at least one `AccountOutput` crediting value to that +account's `consensus_account_id`. + +## Consensus account output bundle + +This ZIP defines a second bundle type for the v7 transaction format. The +consensus account output bundle credits value to consensus accounts. + +### Consensus Account Output Effecting Data + +| Bytes | Name | Data Type | Description | +|---------|-------------|------------------------------|-------------| +| varies | `nOutputs` | `compactSize` | The number of account outputs. | +| varies | `vOutputs` | `AccountOutput[nOutputs]` | The account output records. | + +### AccountOutput + +| Bytes | Name | Data Type | Description | +|---------|--------------|--------------------------|-------------| +| 32 | `accountId` | `byte[32]` | The `consensus_account_id` of the account to credit. | +| 1 | `assetClass` | `uint8` | Asset class identifier. 0x00 for ZEC, 0x01 for other assets. | +| 0 or 64 | `assetId` | `byte[0]` or `byte[64]` | If `assetClass == 0`, the zero-length byte array; otherwise a 64-byte asset identifier. | +| 8 | `value` | `uint64` | The value to credit to the account. | + +Upon processing an `AccountOutput`, full validators: +1. MUST reject the transaction if no account with the given `accountId` exists + (note: registrations in the same transaction are processed first). +2. Add `value` to the account's `balance`. + +### Consensus Account Output Authorizing Data + +The consensus account output bundle has no authorizing data. Any party may +credit value to an existing account (analogous to sending funds to an address). + +### Consensus Account Output Value Pool Delta + +Account outputs remove value from the transparent transaction value pool. The +`mValuePoolDeltas` entry for the consensus account output bundle MUST equal the +negation of the sum of all output values, and that sum MUST be at most +$\mathsf{MAX\_MONEY}$: + +``` +value = -Σ(output.value for each output in vOutputs) +``` + +### Consensus Account Output Digest + +The `bundle_effects_digest` of the consensus account output bundle is a +BLAKE2b-256 hash of the encodings of the elements of `vOutputs`, concatenated +in order, with the personalization field set to `"ZTxIdAcctOutHash"`. + +### Consensus Account Output Consensus Rules + +As of the activation of this ZIP, full validators MUST reject transactions +where any `AccountOutput` has `assetClass` other than 0x00. Support for +crediting other assets to consensus accounts may be added in a future network +upgrade. + +## Consensus account spend bundle + +This ZIP defines a third bundle type for the v7 transaction format: the +consensus account spend bundle. This bundle allows spending value from +consensus accounts into shielded pools. + +### Consensus Account Spend Effecting Data + +| Bytes | Name | Data Type | Description | +|---------|----------------|----------------------------------|-------------| +| varies | `nSpends` | `compactSize` | The number of account spends. | +| varies | `vSpends` | `AccountSpend[nSpends]` | The account spend descriptions. | + +### AccountSpend + +| Bytes | Name | Data Type | Description | +|---------|--------------|--------------------------|-------------| +| 32 | `accountId` | `byte[32]` | The `consensus_account_id` of the account to spend from. | +| varies | `spendKey` | `TrackedKey` | The `application_key` that authorizes this spend, in the encoding defined in ZIP 270. | +| 1 | `assetClass` | `uint8` | Asset class identifier. 0x00 for ZEC, 0x01 for other assets. | +| 0 or 64 | `assetId` | `byte[0]` or `byte[64]` | If `assetClass == 0`, the zero-length byte array; otherwise a 64-byte asset identifier. | +| 8 | `value` | `uint64` | The value to spend from the account. | + +### Consensus Account Spend Authorizing Data + +| Bytes | Name | Data Type | Description | +|---------|----------------|------------------------------|-------------| +| varies | `vSpendAuths` | `AccountSignature[nSpends]` | Authorization signatures for each spend. | + +The `vSpendAuths` entries correspond positionally to `vSpends` entries. Each +signature MUST verify against the `spendKey` of the corresponding +`AccountSpend`. + +### Consensus Account Spend Value Pool Delta + +Account spends remove value from accounts and add it to the transparent +transaction value pool. The `mValuePoolDeltas` entry for the consensus account +spend bundle MUST equal the sum of all spend values, and that sum MUST be at +most $\mathsf{MAX\_MONEY}$: + +``` +value = Σ(spend.value for each spend in vSpends) +``` + +### Consensus Account Spend Digests + +The `bundle_effects_digest` of the consensus account spend bundle is a +BLAKE2b-256 hash of the encodings of the elements of `vSpends`, concatenated in +order, with the personalization field set to `"ZTxIdAcctSpdHash"`. + +Its `bundle_auth_digest` is a BLAKE2b-256 hash of the encodings of the elements +of `vSpendAuths`, concatenated in order, with the personalization field set to +`"ZTxAuthAcSpdHash"`. + +### Consensus Account Spend Consensus Rules + +- A transaction that has an entry for the consensus account spend bundle in + `mEffectBundles` MUST also have one in `mAuthBundles`. +- A coinbase transaction MUST NOT contain a consensus account spend bundle. +- Full validators MUST reject a transaction containing a consensus account + spend bundle if any `AccountSpend` references an `accountId` that does not + exist. +- Full validators MUST reject a transaction if the `spendKey` of any + `AccountSpend` is not the current `application_key` of the account identified + by its `accountId`. +- Full validators MUST reject a transaction if the total value spent from any + single account (summing all `AccountSpend` entries for that account) exceeds + that account's current balance. +- Full validators MUST reject a transaction containing a consensus account + spend bundle if any output within the transaction is not shielded: the + transaction MUST NOT have transparent outputs, and MUST NOT contain a + consensus account output bundle. This preserves the requirement that all + newly-issued ZEC must be shielded at least once before being transferred or + deshielded. +- As of the activation of this ZIP, full validators MUST reject transactions + where any `AccountSpend` has `assetClass` other than 0x00. + +## Changes to ZIP 248 + +In the section 'v7 Transaction Bundle Type Registry' [^zip-0248-registry], add +the following rows, with bundle type identifiers to be allocated in that +registry, and remove the row for lockbox disbursement from 'Potential Future +Bundle Types': + +| BundleType | BundleVariant | `mValuePoolDeltas` | `mEffectBundles` | `mAuthBundles` | Defining ZIP | Bundle kind | +|------------|---------------|--------------------|------------------|----------------|--------------|--------------------------| +| TBD | 0 | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ZIP 272 | Account registration | +| TBD | 0 | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ZIP 272 | Consensus account output | +| TBD | 0 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ZIP 272 | Consensus account spend | + +## Key usage for consensus accounts + +This ZIP defines the key usage `0x01` of ZIP 270, consensus account spending: + +- Its `key_id` is the 32-byte `consensus_account_id`. +- A key pointer is registered when its account is initialized, either by the + consensus rules or by an account registration bundle. +- The `application_key` validates the signatures of the `AccountSpend` entries + for that account. + +## Changes to ZIP 207 + +The following paragraphs are added to the section Funding Streams, after the +definition of Revision 1 recipient identifiers: + +> As of Revision 3, a recipient identifier MAY be a consensus account +> identifier as defined in ZIP 272. +> +> Any funding stream defined after the activation of ZIP 272 MUST use a +> consensus account identifier as its recipient. + +## Changes to ZIP 214 + +The following bullet point is added to the section Revisions: + +> - Revision 3: The Zcash Community Grants funding stream is redirected to a +> consensus account at the activation height of this ZIP. The +> coinholder-controlled fund (dev fund lockbox) continues unchanged. + +The Revision 2 ZCG funding stream (`FS_FPF_ZCG_H2`) ends at the activation +height of this ZIP. A new Revision 3 ZCG funding stream begins at that height, +directing outputs to a ZCG consensus account. + +The following new sections are added: + +> ## Mainnet Recipients for Revision 3 +> +> ``` +> FS_FPF_ZCG_H3 = TODO (consensus account identifier) +> ``` +> +> ## Testnet Recipients for Revision 3 +> +> ``` +> FS_FPF_ZCG_H3 = TODO (consensus account identifier) +> ``` + +## Changes to the Zcash Protocol Specification + +### Section 3.4 (Transactions and Treestates) + +The global chain state is extended to include a map `consensus_accounts` from +`consensus_account_id` to account state, as defined in this ZIP. + +### Section 7.1.2 (Transaction Consensus Rules) + +The consensus rules specified above for the account registration bundle, the +consensus account output bundle, and the consensus account spend bundle are +added. + +### Section 7.8 (Block Subsidy and Founders' Reward) + +Funding stream outputs to consensus accounts are credited via implicit +additions to the `consensus_accounts` map, rather than via explicit transaction +outputs. The value balance of a coinbase transaction is computed to include +these implicit credits. + + +# Rationale + +Implicit rules are kept in the post-rework to reduce churn for miners; they +only need to know the fraction of block subsidy available for miner rewards, +instead of needing to ensure they craft the correct outputs for the current +consensus rules in their block templates. + +Shielded coinbase outputs are retained alongside consensus accounts because +they offer superior privacy properties for miners who desire them. Although the +receiving address of a shielded coinbase output is publicly visible, its +subsequent spend is indistinguishable from other shielded spends. In contrast, +spending from a consensus account is always a publicly visible operation. +Retaining shielded coinbase also avoids forcing privacy-conscious miners to +generate a new consensus account key for each block, which would cause +unbounded growth of the consensus account set. + +Account registration and account outputs are specified as separate bundles +because these operations have fundamentally different characteristics. Account +registrations require a signature proving control of the registered public key; +this prevents the creation of accounts with keys that no one controls, which +would permanently burn any funds credited to them. Account outputs, in +contrast, require no authorization—any party may credit value to an existing +account, analogous to sending funds to a known address. Separating these into +distinct bundles provides a cleaner abstraction: the registration bundle +handles identity establishment (with authorization), while the output bundle +handles value transfer (without authorization). The requirement that a coinbase +transaction with registrations must include outputs to those accounts ensures +that newly registered accounts receive their initial funding in a single atomic +operation. + +Consensus accounts are limited to the recipients of new issuance, and are not a +general-purpose transparent account model. Spending from a consensus account is +authorized by a single signature; accounts do not replicate the scripts by +which spend authority over transparent outputs can be controlled, and because +every spend from an account is shielded, they cannot be used for transparent +payments. + +Accounts need no nonce to prevent a spend from being replayed. A spend +signature commits to the identifier of its transaction, and that transaction +can be mined only once: a v7 transaction that is not a coinbase transaction is +required to spend a transparent output or reveal a nullifier (§ 7.1.2 +'Transaction Consensus Rules' [^protocol-txnconsensus] as modified by ZIP 248), +and this ZIP does not make an account spend count towards that requirement. + + +# Alternatives + +An alternative design considered was a single combined bundle containing both +registrations and credits, with registrations including a value field. This +would result in a single entry in `mValuePoolDeltas`. However, this approach +conflates two distinct operations (identity establishment and value transfer) +and requires either including asset class fields in registrations (adding +complexity) or limiting registrations to ZEC only (reducing future +flexibility). The two-bundle design provides cleaner separation of concerns and +allows the registration bundle to remain simple and focused on key management. + + +# Deployment + +TBD + + +# Reference implementation + +TBD + + +# Open issues + +- The account of the Coinholder-Controlled Fund is not yet specified: its + initial keys, how the balance of the Deferred Dev Fund Lockbox becomes its + balance, and how funding streams with the $\mathsf{DEFERRED\_POOL}$ + recipient credit it. Until it is, this ZIP does not provide disbursement + from the lockbox. +- Consensus account balances are not yet assigned to a chain value pool. One + option is for $\mathsf{ChainValuePoolBalance^{Deferred}}$ to become the sum + of the balances of all consensus accounts. +- The changes to ZIP 207 [^zip-0207] and ZIP 214 [^zip-0214] above predate + NU7, which has since activated. Revision 3 of ZIP 214 is its NU7 revision, + the existing ZCG funding stream is `FS_FPF_ZCG_H3` (not `FS_FPF_ZCG_H2`), and + that stream now ends at the third halving rather than at the height given in + the Requirements. They also assume that the ZCG funding stream continues, + which other draft ZIPs propose to change. [^draft-wind-down-zcg] + [^draft-legal-defense-fund] +- The Abstract says that this ZIP eliminates the coinbase maturity rule. The + Specification does not yet say how that rule applies to funds credited to an + account by a coinbase transaction. +- ZIP 317 [^zip-0317] does not yet say how the bundles defined in this ZIP + contribute to the conventional fee. + + +# References + +[^BCP14]: [Information on BCP 14 — "RFC 2119: Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels" and "RFC 8174: Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words"](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp14) + +[^protocol]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, Version 2025.6.3 [NU6.1] or later](protocol/protocol.pdf) + +[^protocol-blockchain]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, Version 2025.6.3 [NU6.1]. Section 3.3: The Block Chain](protocol/protocol.pdf#blockchain) + +[^protocol-networks]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, Version 2025.6.3 [NU6.1]. Section 3.12: Mainnet and Testnet](protocol/protocol.pdf#networks) + +[^protocol-txnconsensus]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, Version 2025.6.3 [NU6.1]. Section 7.1.2: Transaction Consensus Rules](protocol/protocol.pdf#txnconsensus) + +[^zip-0248]: [ZIP 248: Extensible Transaction Format](zip-0248.rst) + +[^zip-0248-registry]: [ZIP 248: Extensible Transaction Format — v7 Transaction Bundle Type Registry](zip-0248.rst#v7-transaction-bundle-type-registry) + +[^zip-0248-sigdigest]: [ZIP 248: Extensible Transaction Format — Variant 0 Signature Digest](zip-0248.rst#variant-0-signature-digest) + +[^zip-0270]: [ZIP 270: Key Rotation for Tracked Signing Keys](https://github.com/zcash/zips/pull/1473) + +[^zip-0207]: [ZIP 207: Funding Streams](zip-0207.rst) + +[^zip-0214]: [ZIP 214: Consensus rules for a Zcash Development Fund](zip-0214.rst) + +[^zip-0227]: [ZIP 227: Zcash Shielded Assets (ZSA)](zip-0227.md) + +[^zip-0317]: [ZIP 317: Proportional Transfer Fee Mechanism](zip-0317.md) + +[^zip-1016]: [ZIP 1016: Community and Coinholder Funding Model](zip-1016.md) + +[^draft-wind-down-zcg]: [Draft ZIP: Winding Down Zcash Community Grants and Removal of ZCG Funds to the Network Sustainability Mechanism](draft-howard-wind-down-zcg.md) + +[^draft-legal-defense-fund]: [Draft ZIP: Future Dev and Legal Defense Fund Lockbox, and Removal of ZCG Funds to the Network Sustainability Mechanism](draft-mcgee-future-dev-legal-defense-fund.md)

@@ -0,0 +1,136 @@
+    ZIP: Unassigned
+    Title: Limited Block Serving Service Flag
+    Owners: Marek <marek@zfnd.org>
+    Status: Draft
+    Category: Network
+    Created: 2026-11-03
+    License: MIT
+
+
+# Terminology
+
+The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", and "MAY" in this
+document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [^BCP14] when, and only
+when, they appear in all capitals.
+
+best tip
+:   The tip of a node's best block chain.
+
+limited peer
+:   A peer that advertises `NODE_NETWORK_LIMITED` and not `NODE_NETWORK`.
+
+
+# Abstract
+
+This ZIP defines the service flag `NODE_NETWORK_LIMITED` for the Zcash
+peer-to-peer protocol specified in ZIP 204 [^zip-0204]. A node that sets it
+serves at least the most recent 2,304 blocks of its best chain, but not
+necessarily older blocks. It is the Zcash counterpart of BIP 159
+[^bip-0159].
+
+
+# Motivation
+
+A node that deletes old block bodies, such as a Zebra node with pruning
+enabled, cannot set `NODE_NETWORK`, and ZIP 204 defines no other flag for
+serving blocks. Peers cannot tell that such a node serves recent blocks: some
+ignore it, and others request historical blocks it does not have.
+
+The Version 2 P2P protocol draft [^draft-p2p-v2] defines the same flag. This
+ZIP specifies it for the current protocol, so that it can be deployed without
+the rest of that draft.
+
+
+# Specification
+
+## Service Flag
+
+The service flag `NODE_NETWORK_LIMITED` is defined as bit 10
+(`0x0000000000000400`) of the `services` field.
+
+A node that sets `NODE_NETWORK_LIMITED` MUST be able to serve every block of
+its best chain at a height greater than its best tip height minus 2,304, in
+response to `getdata` requests with `MSG_BLOCK`. A node that does not hold all
+of these blocks, for example because it retains fewer than 2,304 blocks or
+started from a recent state snapshot, MUST NOT set it until it does.
+
+A node that cannot serve the complete block chain MUST NOT set `NODE_NETWORK`,
+and SHOULD set `NODE_NETWORK_LIMITED` if it meets the requirement above. A
+node that sets `NODE_NETWORK` MAY also set it.
+
+## Serving
+
+A limited peer SHOULD NOT serve blocks more than 2,304 blocks below its best
+tip, and SHOULD answer requests for them with `notfound`. It MAY disconnect a
+peer that requests a block more than 2,306 blocks below its best tip; the
+2-block margin allows for the best tip advancing while a request is in
+flight.
+
+## Requesting
+
+A node MUST NOT request a block from a limited peer unless it knows the
+block's height from its own validated chain, and that height is within 2,304
+blocks of its own best tip. A block whose parent is in the node's best chain
+has a known height. A block known only by its hash, for example from an `inv`
+message, does not, and the node MUST request it from another peer or learn its
+height first.
+
+A node SHOULD rely on limited peers for blocks only while its best tip is
+within 1,152 blocks of the network's best tip, leaving half of the window for
+chain reorganizations and for differences between the two nodes' best tips.
+It SHOULD send `getblocks` to a limited peer only when the first hash in the
+request's block locator is its own best tip.
+
+## Address Relay
+
+Nodes SHOULD relay addresses advertising `NODE_NETWORK_LIMITED` as they relay
+other addresses.
+
+## Deployment
+
+This ZIP requires no network upgrade. Nodes ignore service flags they do not
+recognize, so a node can set `NODE_NETWORK_LIMITED` as soon as it implements
+this ZIP.
+
+
+# Rationale
+
+Bit 10 and the 2,304-block window match the Version 2 P2P protocol draft
+[^draft-p2p-v2], so a node can advertise the same capability in both
+protocols. Bit 10 is also the bit that BIP 159 assigns to the same capability
+in Bitcoin.
+
+The window is defined in blocks rather than time, so that a peer can check a
+request against it without knowing the block target spacing. At 75, 25 and 10
+seconds per block it covers about 48, 16 and 6.4 hours.
+
+The 1,152-block margin for requesters, and the rule against serving older
+blocks, follow BIP 159's 144-block reorganization buffer and its
+fingerprinting countermeasure. BIP 159 does not specify disconnection; the
+2-block margin follows Bitcoin Core's implementation [^bitcoin-core-limited].
+
+A peer can announce the hash of any block, including one far below the window,
+so a requester checks the window against a height it has validated itself. An
+announcement that carries the block header, such as a compact block, names the
+parent, so a block a limited peer has just mined can still be requested from
+that peer.
+
+
+# Security and Privacy Considerations
+
+A limited peer that served every block it retains would reveal its retention
+depth, which helps distinguish it from other nodes. Serving only the window
+avoids this.
+
+
+# References
+
+[^BCP14]: [Information on BCP 14 — "RFC 2119: Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels" and "RFC 8174: Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words"](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp14)
+
+[^zip-0204]: [ZIP 204: Zcash P2P Network Protocol](zip-0204.rst)
+
+[^bip-0159]: [BIP 159: NODE_NETWORK_LIMITED service bit](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0159.mediawiki)
+
+[^draft-p2p-v2]: [Draft ZIP: Version 2 Zcash P2P Network Protocol](draft-arya-jvff-p2p-quic-transport.md)
+
+[^bitcoin-core-limited]: [Bitcoin Core: block requests below the NODE_NETWORK_LIMITED threshold (`net_processing.cpp`)](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/master/src/net_processing.cpp)

+
+    ZIP: Unassigned
+    Title: Increase the Block Size Limit to 3 MB
+    Owners: Dev Ojha <dev@valargroup.dev>
+            Evan Forbes <evan@valargroup.dev>
+    Status: Draft
+    Category: Consensus
+    Created: 2026-11-06
+    License: MIT
+
+
+# Terminology
+
+The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", and "SHOULD" in this document are to be
+interpreted as described in BCP 14 [^BCP14] when, and only when, they appear
+in all capitals.
+
+The terms "block chain", "consensus branch", and "network upgrade" follow
+ZIP 200. [^zip-0200] Block and transaction encodings follow the Zcash Protocol
+Specification. [^protocol]
+
+MB means 1,000,000 bytes. The existing block
+size limit is 2 MB; this proposal increases it to 3 MB.
+
+"Orphan rate" means distinct observed orphan blocks divided by the sum of
+canonical and observed orphan blocks. Here, an orphan block is a block outside
+the final agreed chain. The experiment below counts a block
+only if at least one node recorded a successful commit. It does not count
+every solved block that a miner discarded before submission.
+
+"Reach 90%" means elapsed time from the miner's solution-ready event to
+decoded block availability at 72 of the experiment's 80 nodes, including
+the originating node at time zero.
+
+
+# Abstract
+
+This proposal increases the block size limit from 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 bytes
+(3 MB) in a network upgrade after NU7. It preserves ZIP 218's shielded action
+limits and shared shielded budget. [^zip-0218] It also preserves the
+2,000,000-byte transaction cap currently enforced by consensus and the existing signature-operation
+limit.
+
+The additional space primarily increases capacity for transparent
+transactions. It prepares the block byte budget for future shielded
+throughput without raising today's shielded scanning burden through an
+action-limit increase. A future proposal to increase shielded action limits
+would depend on adoption and operational validation of private information
+retrieval (PIR), with measured wallet bandwidth and privacy costs.
+
+The proposal also changes block-message size negotiation so that upgraded
+peers can relay valid 3 MB blocks. It leaves block target spacing to separate
+proposals. Larger blocks increase full-node bandwidth, storage, and
+potential validation work.
+
+
+# Motivation
+
+ZIP 218 separates the block byte budget from the shielded action budget.
+The byte budget limits serialized data; the action budget limits shielded
+work and compact sync bandwidth. Its action limits do not apply to the
+transparent components of transactions. [^zip-0218]
+
+With the upcoming Tachyon shielded pool, wallets are intended to use more
+scalable flows, such as out-of-band communication and PIR, to discover
+incoming transactions. Given that, the limiters on the throughput of Zcash
+will be off-chain services and the throughput of consensus itself.
+Increasing the throughput of consensus necessitates increasing the block
+size, lowering the average block time, or both. Under single-chain proof of
+work, it is hard to reduce block times too far because of their high
+variance, hence it is critical to take on the trade-off of larger block
+sizes.
+
+Increasing the byte budget now allows more transparent transactions when
+bytes are the binding constraint. Increasing transparent throughput is an
+intermediate benefit, not Zcash's long-term scaling objective. Deploying
+and measuring larger blocks also prepares the network for future shielded
+throughput once wallets can handle it privately and efficiently.
+
+This proposal separates those decisions. It increases block space while
+retaining all shielded action limits. PIR adoption does not automatically
+activate higher limits; any change requires a separate consensus proposal.
+
+
+# Requirements
+
+- Increase the maximum serialized block size to exactly 3 MB.
+- Preserve historical validity and all existing shielded action limits.
+- Preserve transaction-size, signature-operation, and script limits.
+- Support full-sized blocks through relay, synchronization, and mining.
+- Bound resource use before accepting untrusted block bodies.
+
+
+# Specification
+
+## Activation and block size
+
+Define the following constants:
+
+$$\mathsf{ThreeMBActivationHeight} : \mathbb{N}.$$
+
+$$\mathsf{ThreeMBBlockSizeLimit} : \mathbb{N} := 3\times10^6 = 3{,}000{,}000.$$
+
+A deployment ZIP will assign $\mathsf{ThreeMBActivationHeight}$ for each
+network. It MUST be greater than that network's NU7 activation height.
+Let $A = \mathsf{ThreeMBActivationHeight}$. For block height
+$h \in \mathbb{N}$, define:
+
+$$\mathsf{BlockSizeLimit}(h) := \begin{cases}2{,}000{,}000 & h < A,\\3{,}000{,}000 & h \geq A.\end{cases}$$
+
+Replace the fixed block size bound in § 7.6 'Block Header Encoding and
+Consensus' with the requirement that a block at height $h$ MUST have encoded
+size at most $\mathsf{BlockSizeLimit}(h)$. [^protocol-blockheader]
+
+In the same section, qualify the comparison with Bitcoin's block size limit:
+Zcash's 2,000,000-byte limit applies below $A$; the 3,000,000-byte limit applies
+at or above $A$.
+
+In ZIP 218's specification, replace the statement that the overall 2 MB block
+size limit continues to apply with a reference to $\mathsf{BlockSizeLimit}(h)$
+after this proposal activates. ZIP 218's shielded action limits remain
+unchanged. [^zip-0218]
+
+Encoded size includes the block header, its Equihash solution, the encoded
+transaction count, and every transaction, including the coinbase. It excludes
+the 24-byte P2P message header and storage or RPC wrappers. No field receives
+a size discount.
+
+Validators MUST select the limit using the candidate block's height on its
+parent chain. The local tip height and the peer's advertised height MUST NOT
+determine consensus validity. Validators MUST retain the old limit below
+$A$, including during initial synchronization, side-chain validation, and
+reorganizations across activation.
+
+## Transaction and computational limits
+
+Define $\mathsf{TransactionSizeLimit} : \mathbb{N} := 2{,}000{,}000$ bytes.
+For every block at or above $A$, each transaction, including the coinbase,
+MUST have encoded size at most $\mathsf{TransactionSizeLimit}$.
+Pre-activation transaction rules remain unchanged.
+
+The transaction bound remains independent of the block bound. The additional
+space admits more transactions. zcashd already enforces an explicit
+2,000,000-byte transaction cap. The protocol specification states a
+100,000-byte cap before Sapling; after Sapling, the block envelope also
+limits the size of any included transaction. This proposal makes the
+independent 2,000,000-byte post-activation transaction cap explicit, so
+increasing the block envelope does not admit larger individual transactions.
+[^zcashd-limits] [^protocol]
+
+The block signature-operation limit remains 20,000, using the existing
+counting rules, including P2SH signature operations. Existing script limits
+and transaction-format bounds remain unchanged. [^zcashd-limits]
+
+This proposal does not change block target spacing, but benchmarks for safety
+are done with 20-second target spacing in mind.
+
+## Block relay and message framing
+
+ZIP 204 currently limits each message payload to 2,097,152 bytes. That limit
+cannot carry a valid 3 MB block. Amend its 'Maximum Message Size' rules as
+follows. [^zip-0204]
+
+Define $\mathsf{ThreeMBProtocolVersion} : \mathbb{N}$, to be assigned by the
+deployment ZIP. For a connection whose negotiated protocol version is at
+least this value, the maximum `block` message payload is 3,000,000 bytes.
+For older negotiated versions, retain the 2,097,152-byte maximum. Other
+commands retain their existing payload and item-count limits.
+
+Nodes MUST reject a declared payload length above the applicable maximum
+before allocating a buffer for that payload. A decoder MUST consume exactly
+one block from a `block` payload and reject trailing data, truncated fields,
+and invalid encodings. Existing checksum checks remain in force.
+
+Upgraded nodes MUST support the larger `block` payload on upgraded
+connections even when their local tip is below $A$. They still apply the
+height-dependent consensus bound when validating the block. This permits
+initial synchronization and out-of-order delivery across activation without
+accepting oversized pre-activation blocks.
+
+Senders MUST NOT send a payload above the peer connection's negotiated
+maximum. The deployment MUST update minimum peer versions and apply
+ZIP 201's upgrade peer-management rules so that upgraded nodes can retain
+compatible peers at activation. [^zip-0201]
+
+## Mining and node interfaces
+
+`getblocktemplate` MUST report `sizelimit` for the candidate height, normally
+one above the selected parent. Template selection MUST reserve space for
+the complete header, encoded transaction count, and completed coinbase.
+Miners MUST re-evaluate the limit when a parent change crosses activation.
+
+Block submission and retrieval interfaces MUST support every otherwise-valid
+block within the applicable limit. This includes proposal validation, RPC
+submission, historical retrieval, and local block import.
+
+Deserializers MUST distinguish the block envelope limit from transaction
+and field limits. Increasing the block limit MUST NOT implicitly increase
+`tx`, inventory, address, or header-message limits. Nodes SHOULD bound
+aggregate queued block bytes and decoded memory, rather than relying only
+on a count of blocks or connections.
+
+This proposal does not increase mempool memory defaults or change ZIP 317's
+fee calculation. ZIP 401's cost limit remains a node resource policy, not a
+fixed entitlement to a number of full blocks. [^zip-0317] [^zip-0401]
+
+
+# Rationale
+
+## Choice of block size
+
+The authors chose 3 MB because, at that size, current Zakura and Zebra Andale
+implementations keep orphan rates below Ethereum's historical average of
+5.4%. The experiment below provides preliminary Zakura evidence near that size.
+
+## Throughput and resource costs
+
+The new byte budget is $3{,}000{,}000/2{,}000{,}000 = 1.5$ times the old
+budget, an increase of 50%. Transaction throughput depends
+on the workload. Transparent transactions can use the additional space,
+but signature operations, script execution, and UTXO access can become
+binding constraints. Action-limited shielded workloads do not receive a
+corresponding increase in transactions per block.
+
+The following bounds assume every canonical block reaches 3 MB and blocks
+arrive at the stated target spacing:
+
+| Target spacing | Raw block payload rate | Raw block data per day | Capacity relative to 2 MB at 25 seconds |
+|----------------|------------------------|------------------------|----------------------------------------|
+| 25 seconds | 120,000 bytes/second | 10.368 GB | 1.5× |
+| 20 seconds | 150,000 bytes/second | 12.96 GB | 1.875× |
+
+These figures exclude repeated relay, orphan blocks, transport overhead,
+indexes, and state growth. They describe full-block traffic, not light-wallet
+compact sync. Disk and memory costs can grow differently from serialized
+bytes, especially for blocks with many small transparent outputs.
+
+Keeping the 20,000 signature-operation limit bounds counted operations; it
+does not bound all validation work. Transparent-heavy blocks require
+measurements of script execution, UTXO reads and writes, memory, and
+validation-to-mining-tip latency.
+
+## Propagation experiment
+
+A November 2026 private-network experiment used 80 Zakura nodes across 12
+regions at a 20-second target spacing. Blocks filled twice ZIP 218's normal
+shielded action limit: 660 Ironwood actions. The measured blocks occupied
+3,026,379 bytes, approximately 3 MB and slightly above the proposed limit.
+
+| Measurement | Mean | Median | 95th percentile |
+|-------------|------|--------|-----------------|
+| Block propagation to 90% of nodes | 1.20 s | 1.02 s | 2.18 s |
+
+The observed orphan rate was **3.6%**.
+
+**TODO:** Report propagation to 90% of nodes using a mixed Zakura / Zebra Andale
+network.
+
+
+## Computation and I/O benchmarks
+
+The original Zcash block-size increase prompted analysis of verification
+costs across different input/output mixes. [^zcashd-worst-case] A fixed
+signature-operation limit does not capture every validation cost.
+
+Before deployment, benchmark the following workloads at the proposed limit:
+
+| Workload | Costs to examine |
+|----------|------------------|
+| Many small transparent transactions | Per-transaction overhead and UTXO lookups |
+| Output-heavy transparent transactions | UTXO growth and database writes |
+| Signature-heavy transparent transactions | Signature verification and script execution |
+| Mixed transparent and shielded transactions | Combined UTXO and proof-verification work under unchanged action limits |
+
+For each workload, report validation-to-mining-tip time, UTXO reads and writes,
+and peak memory. Record client version, hardware, and cache conditions so
+others can reproduce the results.
+
+
+# Deployment
+
+Deploy through a network upgrade after NU7. A deployment ZIP will assign
+activation heights, consensus branch IDs, and the new protocol version.
+This proposal can activate with a separately specified spacing change, but
+does not require a 20-second target.
+
+Before advancing to Proposed status, publish reproducible experiment inputs
+and resolve the deployment assignments. Validate the byte and computational
+boundaries across independent clients. Run matched 3 MB transparent and
+mixed workloads at the selected spacing, including constrained bandwidth,
+propagation tails, orphan blocks, UTXO growth, and mining-tip adoption.
+
+
+# References
+
+[^BCP14]: [Information on BCP 14](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp14)
+
+[^protocol]: [Zcash Protocol Specification](protocol/protocol.pdf)
+
+[^protocol-blockheader]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, § 7.6: Block Header Encoding and Consensus](protocol/protocol.pdf#blockheader)
+
+[^zip-0200]: [ZIP 200: Network Upgrade Mechanism](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0200)
+
+[^zip-0201]: [ZIP 201: Network Peer Management for Overwinter](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0201)
+
+[^zip-0204]: [ZIP 204: Zcash P2P Network Protocol](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0204)
+
+[^zip-0218]: [ZIP 218: 25-second Block Target Spacing](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0218)
+
+[^zip-0317]: [ZIP 317: Proportional Transfer Fee Mechanism](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0317)
+
+[^zip-0401]: [ZIP 401: Addressing Mempool Denial-of-Service](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0401)
+
+[^zcashd-limits]: [zcashd: consensus limits](https://github.com/zcash/zcash/blob/master/src/consensus/consensus.h)
+
+[^zcashd-worst-case]: [zcashd issue #1077: Worst-case block verification costs](https://github.com/zcash/zcash/issues/1077)
