@@ -0,0 +1,386 @@
+    ZIP: Unassigned
+    Title: Compact Block Relay
+    Owners: Marek <marek@zfnd.org>
+    Status: Draft
+    Category: Network
+    Created: 2026-10-30
+    License: MIT
+    Discussions-To: <https://github.com/zcash/zips/issues/360>
+
+
+# Terminology
+
+The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "SHOULD", and "MAY" in this document are to
+be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [^BCP14] when, and only when, they appear
+in all capitals.
+
+The terms "Mainnet" and "Testnet" are to be interpreted as described in
+section 3.12 of the Zcash Protocol Specification. [^protocol-networks]
+
+The terms "txid", "authorizing data commitment" (denoted `auth_digest`), and
+"witnessed transaction identifier" ("wtxid") are to be interpreted as
+described in ZIP 239. [^zip-0239]
+
+best tip
+:   The tip of a node's best fully validated block chain.
+
+early relay
+:   Announcing or sending a block before the sending node has fully validated
+    it.
+
+authenticated block
+:   A block that passes the checks in [Early Relay].
+
+
+# Abstract
+
+This ZIP specifies compact block relay for the Zcash peer-to-peer network,
+adapted from BIP 152. [^bip-0152] A compact block contains the block header,
+short identifiers for the block's transactions, and its coinbase transaction;
+the receiver reconstructs the block from transactions it already has. Peers
+that both opt in may also relay a block before fully validating it, once its
+header and transaction commitments have been checked.
+
+
+# Motivation
+
+As in Bitcoin before BIP 152, a Zcash node announces a block only after fully
+validating it, and a peer that requests the block receives every transaction
+in it, although it has usually already received most of them through
+transaction relay. Both delay the propagation of new blocks between miners.
+
+BIP 152 replaces transactions the receiver already has with short
+identifiers, and allows a block to be relayed before it is fully validated.
+It cannot be used in Zcash unchanged: Zcash block headers include an Equihash
+solution, and since NU5 a transaction's txid does not commit to its
+authorizing data [^zip-0244], so short identifiers and the checks made before
+early relay need to cover the wtxid.
+
+
+# Specification
+
+All messages defined in this ZIP are serialized in the standard encoding for
+P2P messages. [^zip-0204]
+
+## Service Flag
+
+The service flag `NODE_COMPACT_BLOCKS` is defined as bit 16
+(`0x0000000000010000`).
+
+A node that sets `NODE_COMPACT_BLOCKS` in its `version` message supports the
+messages defined in this ZIP and follows the rules in [Early Relay] and
+[Peer Misbehaviour].
+
+The messages defined in this ZIP MUST NOT be sent on a connection unless both
+peers set `NODE_COMPACT_BLOCKS` in their `version` messages, and MUST NOT be
+sent before the `version`/`verack` handshake completes. Support MUST NOT be
+inferred from any other source, such as `addr` records, user agents, or
+protocol versions. A node MUST ignore these messages on other connections.
+
+## `sendcmpct`
+
+The `sendcmpct` message is defined as a message where the `command` field is
+(NUL-padded) `"sendcmpct"`, with the following payload:
+
+| Bytes | Name | Data Type | Description |
+|-------|------|-----------|-------------|
+| 1 | `announce` | `uint8` | 1 to request `cmpctblock` announcements, 0 to stop them. |
+| 8 | `version` | `uint64` | Compact block encoding version. |
+
+This ZIP specifies version 1. A message with `announce` other than 0 or 1 is
+malformed.
+
+A node MAY send `cmpctblock` messages to a peer only while the most recent
+`sendcmpct` received from that peer has `announce` = 1 and `version` = 1. A
+`sendcmpct` with any other version disables announcements to its sender, and
+is not a protocol violation.
+
+A node MUST NOT request announcements from more than three peers at a time. It
+SHOULD request them from the peers that most recently first announced blocks
+it then added to its best chain; announcements of blocks it has not validated
+MUST NOT be counted. A node MUST ignore `cmpctblock` messages it has not
+requested. Disabling announcements MUST NOT cancel an outstanding
+`getblocktxn` request.
+
+There is no low-bandwidth mode and no compact block inventory type. Blocks
+are requested with `getdata` and `MSG_BLOCK`, as before.
+
+## `cmpctblock`
+
+The `cmpctblock` message is defined as a message where the `command` field is
+(NUL-padded) `"cmpctblock"`, with the following payload:
+
+| Bytes | Name | Data Type | Description |
+|-------|------|-----------|-------------|
+| varies | `header` | Block header | Encoded as in section 7.6 of the Zcash Protocol Specification. [^protocol-blockheader] |
+| 8 | `nonce` | `uint64` | Nonce used to compute short IDs. |
+| varies | `shortidsCount` | `CompactSize` | Number of short IDs. |
+| `6 * shortidsCount` | `shortids` | `uint8[6][]` | Short IDs of the transactions that are not prefilled, in block order. |
+| varies | `prefilledCount` | `CompactSize` | Number of prefilled transactions. |
+| varies | `prefilled` | `PrefilledTransaction[]` | Prefilled transactions, in block order. |
+
+The header includes the Equihash solution, and does not include the
+transaction count that follows it in a `headers` message. On Mainnet and
+Testnet it is 1,487 bytes.
+
+A `PrefilledTransaction` has the following format:
+
+| Bytes | Name | Data Type | Description |
+|-------|------|-----------|-------------|
+| varies | `index` | `CompactSize` | Differentially encoded index of the transaction in the block. |
+| varies | `tx` | Transaction | The transaction, encoded as in section 7.1 of the Zcash Protocol Specification. [^protocol-txnencoding] |
+
+In a list of differentially encoded indexes, the first entry is the absolute
+index, and each later entry is the absolute index minus the previous absolute
+index minus 1. For example, `[0, 0, 2]` encodes the absolute indexes
+`[0, 1, 4]`. Counts and indexes MUST be checked before allocation or
+indexing, and count addition and index decoding MUST NOT overflow.
+
+Let `n = shortidsCount + prefilledCount` be the number of transactions in the
+block. A node MUST reject a `cmpctblock` message if:
+
+- any of `shortidsCount`, `prefilledCount`, and `n` exceeds 37,037;
+- the absolute prefilled indexes are not strictly increasing, or any is not
+  less than `n`;
+- the first prefilled transaction is not a coinbase transaction at index 0,
+  or any other prefilled transaction is a coinbase transaction; or
+- the sizes of the header, the `CompactSize` encoding of `n`, and the
+  prefilled transactions, plus 54 bytes for each short ID, sum to more than
+  2,000,000 bytes.
+
+Senders SHOULD prefill only the coinbase transaction.
+
+### Short Transaction IDs
+
+The sender SHOULD choose `nonce` uniformly at random for each `cmpctblock`
+message. The short ID of a transaction is computed as follows:
+
+1. Let `h` be the SHA-256 hash of the encoded block header followed by
+   `nonce`.
+2. Let `k0` and `k1` be bytes 0 to 7 and 8 to 15 of `h`, each interpreted as
+   a little-endian `uint64`.
+3. Compute SipHash-2-4 with keys `(k0, k1)` of the transaction's 32-byte txid
+   for v4 and earlier transactions, or of its 64-byte wtxid for v5 and later
+   transactions.
+4. The short ID is the first 6 bytes of the little-endian encoding of the
+   result.
+
+## `getblocktxn` and `blocktxn`
+
+The `getblocktxn` message is defined as a message where the `command` field
+is (NUL-padded) `"getblocktxn"`, with the following payload:
+
+| Bytes | Name | Data Type | Description |
+|-------|------|-----------|-------------|
+| 32 | `blockHash` | `uint8[32]` | Hash of the block announced by `cmpctblock`. |
+| varies | `indexesCount` | `CompactSize` | Number of requested transactions. |
+| varies | `indexes` | `CompactSize[]` | Differentially encoded indexes of the requested transactions. |
+
+The `indexesCount` field MUST NOT exceed 37,037, and the absolute indexes
+MUST be strictly increasing and less than `n`.
+
+The `blocktxn` message is defined as a message where the `command` field is
+(NUL-padded) `"blocktxn"`, with the following payload:
+
+| Bytes | Name | Data Type | Description |
+|-------|------|-----------|-------------|
+| 32 | `blockHash` | `uint8[32]` | `blockHash` from the request. |
+| varies | `txCount` | `CompactSize` | Number of transactions. |
+| varies | `tx` | Transaction[] | The requested transactions, in the order requested. |
+
+A `blocktxn` message MUST contain exactly the requested transactions, which
+MUST NOT exceed 2,000,000 bytes in total.
+
+A node that sends a `cmpctblock` message MUST be able to answer a
+`getblocktxn` request for any subset of the block's transactions, and SHOULD
+retain the block for this purpose for 15 seconds. It SHOULD limit the
+`blocktxn` messages it sends for one `cmpctblock` message, including repeated
+and empty responses, to 2,000,000 bytes in total, and MAY ignore requests
+beyond that limit or after that time. It MUST ignore requests for blocks it
+has not announced on that connection or no longer retains, and requests for
+indexes outside the block.
+
+A node MUST ignore a `blocktxn` message that does not answer its outstanding
+`getblocktxn` request on that connection, and SHOULD wait at most two seconds
+for the answer.
+
+## Sending Compact Blocks
+
+A node MUST send each block announcement as `cmpctblock` to at most three
+peers, and SHOULD do so only when the `cmpctblock` message is smaller than the
+block. Other peers receive the announcement as before. A node MAY announce a
+fully validated block with `cmpctblock` to any peer that requested
+announcements.
+
+### Early Relay
+
+A node MAY relay a block before fully validating it only to peers that set
+`NODE_COMPACT_BLOCKS`, and only after checking that:
+
+- NU5 is active at the block's height;
+- the block's parent is the node's best tip, and the block's coinbase height
+  is one more than the best tip's height;
+- the header has the expected difficulty, a valid Equihash solution, a hash
+  that meets its target, and a valid time with respect to both the local
+  clock and the median time past;
+- the block is at most 2,000,000 bytes, its first transaction is a coinbase
+  transaction, and no later transaction has a transparent input with a null
+  previous output;
+- the block passes the shielded action limits, and the subsidy and funding
+  stream checks that do not depend on value pool state;
+- the txids are distinct and reproduce `hashMerkleRoot`, and each
+  transaction's consensus branch ID is valid at the block's height;
+- the `auth_digest` values of all transactions reproduce the authorizing data
+  root, which together with the parent's chain history reproduces
+  `hashBlockCommitments`, as specified in ZIP 244; [^zip-0244] and
+- the block has not been rejected or invalidated by the node.
+
+While it completes validation, the node MAY announce the block, and MAY answer
+`getdata` requests for it from those peers. It MUST stop early relay of the
+block when its validation fails or is cancelled, or when its parent is no
+longer the best tip, and MUST check these conditions before sending each
+message. It SHOULD continue to answer `getblocktxn` requests for a
+`cmpctblock` message it has already sent.
+
+## Receiving Compact Blocks
+
+Before retaining a `cmpctblock` message or querying its mempool, a node MUST
+check the coinbase height, NU5 activation, the header's time, target, and
+proof of work, and that the block's parent is its best tip. If these checks
+fail, the node SHOULD treat the message as an announcement of the block hash.
+A node SHOULD limit the compact blocks it retains and the `getblocktxn`
+requests it sends, both per peer and in total.
+
+The node then reconstructs the block:
+
+1. Place the prefilled transactions at their indexes.
+2. For each index that is not prefilled, if its short ID occurs only once in
+   the message and exactly one mempool transaction has that short ID, place
+   that transaction at the index.
+3. If any index remains empty, send one `getblocktxn` request for all of
+   them.
+4. Check that the `blocktxn` response contains one transaction for each
+   requested index, with the corresponding short ID.
+5. Check the block size, the coinbase transaction, that the txids are
+   distinct and reproduce `hashMerkleRoot`, and that the `auth_digest` values
+   reproduce the commitments as in [Early Relay], then fully validate the
+   block.
+
+Step 5 is required because a short ID can match the wrong transaction, and
+`hashMerkleRoot` does not commit to authorizing data.
+
+If any step fails, or the response does not arrive in time, the node MUST
+request the block from the same peer with `getdata` and `MSG_BLOCK`, using its
+usual timeout. A reconstruction failure MUST NOT cause the node to treat the
+block as invalid.
+
+## Peer Misbehaviour
+
+A node MAY treat a malformed message defined in this ZIP as it treats other
+malformed P2P messages. This includes non-canonical `CompactSize` encodings,
+indexes out of range, and counts or sizes that exceed the limits above.
+
+A node MUST NOT penalize a peer for short ID collisions, failed
+reconstructions, commitment mismatches in reconstructed blocks, `blocktxn`
+timeouts, or an unknown parent.
+
+A node MUST NOT penalize a peer that set `NODE_COMPACT_BLOCKS` when an
+authenticated block it sent fails later validation; the node still rejects
+the block. A node MAY penalize a peer that sends a full block failing the
+proof of work, size, structure, or commitment checks in [Early Relay]. If the
+node cannot authenticate a block because the parent's chain history is
+unavailable, but the block passes the checks that do not depend on it, the
+node MUST NOT penalize the peer for a later transaction or contextual
+validation failure. Failures of local time policy and local invalidation are
+not peer misbehaviour.
+
+## Deployment
+
+This ZIP applies on Mainnet and Testnet from NU5 activation. It does not
+require a network upgrade. Peers that do not set `NODE_COMPACT_BLOCKS` use
+block relay as before.
+
+
+# Rationale
+
+This ZIP differs from BIP 152 as follows:
+
+- The header is the Zcash block header, including the Equihash solution.
+- Short IDs are computed from the wtxid for v5 and later transactions, so
+  version 1 of the encoding is not Bitcoin's version 1.
+- Only high-bandwidth announcements are defined.
+- Support is signalled by a service flag rather than a protocol version, and
+  an unsupported version disables announcements rather than being negotiated.
+- The coinbase transaction is always prefilled, and all counts and sizes are
+  bounded.
+- Early relay requires checking authorizing data, and is limited to children
+  of the best tip.
+
+Zebra and zcashd ignore unknown P2P messages after the handshake
+[^zebra-codec] [^zcashd-messages], so a service flag is not needed to avoid
+disconnection. It is needed because both peers have to agree on the encoding,
+and on not penalizing authenticated blocks that fail later validation; an
+ignored message establishes neither. A protocol version signals support for a
+network upgrade, not for an optional relay policy. [^zip-0201]
+
+The limit of 37,037 transactions is the 2,000,000-byte block size limit
+divided by 54 bytes, a lower bound on the size of a transaction.
+
+Bit 16 avoids the service flags allocated in Zcash and Bitcoin
+[^bitcoin-services], the range 24 to 31 reserved for temporary experiments,
+and bits 12 to 14, which are used by pending Bitcoin proposals.
+[^bitcoin-utreexo] [^bitcoin-utxo-sharing]
+
+
+# Security and Privacy Considerations
+
+A short ID identifies a transaction only probabilistically. A node that
+skipped the checks in step 5 of [Receiving Compact Blocks] could accept a
+block whose authorizing data differs from the data committed to by its
+header.
+
+An early relayed block can be invalid. Receiving one does not indicate that
+the block is valid, and nodes MUST fully validate it before accepting it.
+
+A `getblocktxn` request reveals which transactions the sender did not have,
+and the timing of announcements can reveal a node's peers. Setting
+`NODE_COMPACT_BLOCKS` reveals that a node supports this ZIP.
+
+
+# Reference Implementation
+
+Zebra implements this ZIP with the option `compact_block_relay`, on by
+default. [^zebra]
+
+
+# References
+
+[^BCP14]: [Information on BCP 14 — "RFC 2119: Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels" and "RFC 8174: Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words"](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp14)
+

+
+[^protocol-txnencoding]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, Version 2026.8.0 [NU6.3]. Section 7.1: Transaction Encoding and Consensus](protocol/protocol.pdf#txnencoding)
+
+[^protocol-blockheader]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, Version 2026.8.0 [NU6.3]. Section 7.6: Block Header Encoding and Consensus](protocol/protocol.pdf#blockheader)
+
+[^zip-0201]: [ZIP 201: Network Peer Management for Overwinter](zip-0201.rst)
+
+[^zip-0204]: [ZIP 204: Zcash P2P Network Protocol](zip-0204.rst)
+
+[^zip-0239]: [ZIP 239: Relay of Version 5 Transactions](zip-0239.rst)
+
+[^zip-0244]: [ZIP 244: Transaction Identifier Non-Malleability](zip-0244.rst)
+
+[^bip-0152]: [BIP 152: Compact Block Relay](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0152.mediawiki)
+
+[^zebra]: [Zebra pull request #12186: negotiate compact block relay with its ZIP service bit, on by default](https://github.com/ZcashFoundation/zebra/pull/12186)

prs.title: Add draft ZIP: 10-second Block Target Spacing
prs.author: upbqdn
prs.bodyExcerpt: [Rendered.](https://github.com/upbqdn/zips/blob/10s-block-target-spacing/zips/draft-marek-10s-block-target-spacing.md) Proposes reducing the block target spacing from 25 seconds (ZIP 218, NU7) to 10 seconds in NU8. The change is limited to latency. The block subsidy, halving interval, funding-stream

files.patch: @@ -239,6 +239,7 @@ be deleted. draft-ecc-authenticated-reply-addrs Authenticated Reply Addresses zips#1230 draft-ecc-onchain-accountable-voting On-chain Accountable Voting draft-emersonian-zcash-town-square The Zcash Town Square: Official Discussion and Announcement Cross-Posting https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/zip-the-zcash-town-square/59049 + draft-marek-10s-block-target-spacing 10-second Block Target Spacing draft-mcgee-future-dev-legal-defense-fund Future Dev and Legal Defense Fund Lockbox, and Removal of ZCG Funds to the Network Sustainability Mechanism https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/future-dev-and-legal-defense-fund-zip/58611 draft-mcgee-keyholders-organizations Update to ZIP 1016 & ZIP 271: Key-Holder Organizations URL TBD draft-str4d-orchard-balance-proof Air drops, Proof-of-Balance, and Stake-weighted Polling zips#1229

@@ -0,0 +1,279 @@
+    ZIP: Unassigned
+    Title: 10-second Block Target Spacing
+    Owners: Marek <marek@zfnd.org>
+    Status: Draft
+    Category: Consensus
+    Created: 2026-10-31
+    License: MIT
+
+
+# Terminology
+
+The key words "MUST", "SHALL", "SHOULD", and "SHOULD NOT" in this document are
+to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [^BCP14] when, and only when, they
+appear in all capitals.
+
+The term "network upgrade" is to be interpreted as defined in ZIP 200.
+[^zip-0200]
+
+The term "block target spacing" is to be interpreted as defined in ZIP 218.
+[^zip-0218]
+
+The character § is used when referring to sections of the Zcash Protocol
+Specification. [^protocol]
+
+The terms "Mainnet" and "Testnet" are to be interpreted as described in
+§ 3.12 'Mainnet and Testnet'. [^protocol-networks]
+
+"NU8" is the code name of the network upgrade that deploys this proposal.
+
+
+# Abstract
+
+This proposal changes the block target spacing from 25 seconds to 10 seconds
+in NU8. The block subsidy, the block size limit, and the shielded action limits
+of each block are scaled by the same factor, so that issuance, block space, and
+shielded capacity per unit of time are unchanged.
+
+
+# Motivation
+
+ZIP 218 reduces the block target spacing from 75 seconds to 25 seconds in NU7
+in order to reduce transaction latency. [^zip-0218] This proposal reduces it to
+10 seconds, which reduces the expected time to a first confirmation from 25
+seconds to 10 seconds.
+
+The proposal changes latency only. Each quantity that NU7 specifies per unit of
+time is preserved: issuance, funding stream address periods, reissuance by the
+Network Sustainability Mechanism, the duration of the difficulty averaging
+window, and the resource limits of the block chain.
+
+
+# Specification
+
+The changes below are made to the Zcash Protocol Specification [^protocol] and
+to ZIPs 207, 214, and 237 [^zip-0207] [^zip-0214] [^zip-0237], as amended for
+NU7 by ZIP 218 [^zip-0218] and ZIP 259 [^zip-0259].
+
+## Block target spacing
+
+In § 5.3 'Constants' [^protocol-constants], define:
+
+$$\mathsf{NU8ActivationHeight} : \mathbb{N}$$
+$$\mathsf{PostNU8PoWTargetSpacing} : \mathbb{N} := 10 \textsf{ seconds}$$
+
+In § 7.7.3 'Difficulty adjustment' [^protocol-diffadjustment], define:
+
+$$\mathsf{NU8PoWTargetSpacingRatio} : \mathbb{Q} := \mathsf{PostNU7PoWTargetSpacing} \;/\; \mathsf{PostNU8PoWTargetSpacing} = 5/2$$
+
+$$\mathsf{IsNU8Activated} : \mathbb{N} \to \{\mathsf{false}, \mathsf{true}\}$$
+$$\mathsf{IsNU8Activated}(\mathsf{height}) := (\mathsf{height} \geq \mathsf{NU8ActivationHeight})$$
+
+On each network, $\mathsf{NU8ActivationHeight}$ SHALL be even.
+
+In the definition of $\mathsf{PoWTargetSpacing}$ in ZIP 218, replace the case
+"otherwise" with "if $\mathsf{IsNU7Activated}(\mathsf{height})$ and not
+$\mathsf{IsNU8Activated}(\mathsf{height})$", and add the case
+$\mathsf{PostNU8PoWTargetSpacing}$ "otherwise".
+
+## Difficulty averaging window
+
+In § 5.3 'Constants', define:
+
+$$\mathsf{PostNU8PoWAveragingWindow} : \mathbb{N} := 255$$
+
+In the definition of $\mathsf{PoWAveragingWindow}$ in ZIP 218, replace the case
+"otherwise" with "if $\mathsf{IsNU7Activated}(\mathsf{height})$ and not
+$\mathsf{IsNU8Activated}(\mathsf{height})$", and add the case
+$\mathsf{PostNU8PoWAveragingWindow}$ "otherwise".
+
+The averaging window timespan therefore remains 2,550 seconds.
+
+## Halving interval and block subsidy
+
+Define:
+
+$$\mathsf{PostNU8HalvingInterval} : \mathbb{N} := \mathsf{PostNU7HalvingInterval} \cdot \mathsf{NU8PoWTargetSpacingRatio} = 12{,}600{,}000$$
+
+In the definition of $\mathsf{Halving}$ in ZIP 218, replace the case
+"otherwise" with "if $\mathsf{IsNU7Activated}(\mathsf{height})$ and not
+$\mathsf{IsNU8Activated}(\mathsf{height})$", and add the case:
+
+$$
+\left\lfloor \dfrac{\mathsf{BlossomActivationHeight} - \mathsf{SlowStartShift}}{\mathsf{PreBlossomHalvingInterval}}
+  + \dfrac{\mathsf{NU7ActivationHeight} - \mathsf{BlossomActivationHeight}}{\mathsf{PostBlossomHalvingInterval}}
+  + \dfrac{\mathsf{NU8ActivationHeight} - \mathsf{NU7ActivationHeight}}{\mathsf{PostNU7HalvingInterval}}
+  + \dfrac{\mathsf{height} - \mathsf{NU8ActivationHeight}}{\mathsf{PostNU8HalvingInterval}} \right\rfloor,
+  \quad \textsf{otherwise}
+$$
+
+In the definition of $\mathsf{ScheduledBlockSubsidy}$ in ZIP 237, replace the
+condition "if $\mathsf{IsNU7Activated}(\mathsf{height})$" of the case added by
+ZIP 218 with "if $\mathsf{IsNU7Activated}(\mathsf{height})$ and not
+$\mathsf{IsNU8Activated}(\mathsf{height})$", and add the case:
+
+$$
+\mathsf{floor}\left(\dfrac{\mathsf{MaxBlockSubsidy}}{\mathsf{BlossomPoWTargetSpacingRatio} \cdot \mathsf{NU7PoWTargetSpacingRatio} \cdot \mathsf{NU8PoWTargetSpacingRatio} \cdot 2^{\mathsf{Halving}(\mathsf{height})}}\right),
+  \quad \textsf{if } \mathsf{IsNU8Activated}(\mathsf{height})
+$$
+
+The denominator is $15 \cdot 2^{\mathsf{Halving}(\mathsf{height})}$.
+
+## Block size and shielded action limits
+
+For a block at a height for which $\mathsf{IsNU8Activated}(\mathsf{height})$,
+the size of the block MUST be less than or equal to 800,000 bytes, in place of
+the limit of 2,000,000 bytes in § 7.6 'Block Header Encoding and Consensus'.
+[^protocol-blockheader]
+
+For such a block, the shielded action limits of ZIP 218 apply with
+$\mathsf{GlobalShieldedBudget} = 132$,
+$\mathsf{OrchardProtocolBlockActionLimit} = 132$, and
+$\mathsf{SaplingBlockIOLimit} = 120$. $\mathsf{SproutBlockJoinSplitLimit}$
+remains 0.
+
+## Funding streams
+
+Let $A$, $R$, $C$, $I$, and $H_1$ be as in the definition of
+$\mathsf{AddressPeriod}$ in Revision 2 of ZIP 207, and let
+$B = \mathsf{NU8ActivationHeight}$. In that definition, replace the case
+"otherwise" with "if $\mathsf{IsNU7Activated}(\mathsf{height})$ and not
+$\mathsf{IsNU8Activated}(\mathsf{height})$", and add the case:
+
+$$
+\mathsf{floor}\left(\dfrac{5\left(R(A + I - H_1) + B - A\right) + 2(\mathsf{height} - B)}{5RC}\right),
+  \quad \textsf{otherwise}
+$$
+
+This preserves the address index at NU8 activation. Each later address period
+lasts $5RC/2 = 262{,}500$ blocks.
+
+For each funding stream that is active at $B$ and whose end height is
+$\mathsf{HeightForHalving}(3)$ by Revision 3 of ZIP 214, the end height SHALL
+be $\mathsf{HeightForHalving}(3)$ calculated using the $\mathsf{Halving}$
+function of this proposal. If $H_3$ is the third-halving height under ZIP 218
+(6,132,390 on Mainnet and 4,497,948 on Testnet), this end height is
+$B + 5(H_3 - B)/2$. The number of addresses that ZIP 207 requires
+for each such stream is unchanged.
+
+## Network Sustainability Mechanism
+
+In ZIP 237, $\mathsf{HalvingInterval}(\mathsf{height})$ is
+$\mathsf{PostNU8HalvingInterval}$ if $\mathsf{IsNU8Activated}(\mathsf{height})$.
+From NU8 activation, $\mathsf{BLOCK\_SUBSIDY\_FRACTION}$ is therefore
+$550 / 10^{10}$.
+
+If $B$ is less than the $\mathsf{DEPLOYMENT\_BLOCK\_HEIGHT}$ that ZIP 237
+specifies for a network, then $\mathsf{DEPLOYMENT\_BLOCK\_HEIGHT}$ for that
+network SHALL instead be calculated as in ZIP 237, with $B$ in place of $A$,
+with $\mathsf{ScheduledBlockSubsidy}$, $H_3$, and $H_4$ as specified by this
+proposal, and with 550 in place of 1375. NU8 activation heights SHALL be chosen
+so that this height exists before $H_4$. The NU8 deployment ZIP specifies the
+resulting height for each network.
+
+## Minimum-difficulty blocks on Testnet
+
+On Testnet, from NU8 activation, the minimum-difficulty threshold specified by
+ZIP 218 is $45 \cdot \mathsf{PoWTargetSpacing}(\mathsf{height})$ seconds, which
+remains 450 seconds.
+
+## Unchanged consensus rules
+
+Consensus rules that are expressed in blocks and not changed above, including
+the coinbase maturity of 100 blocks and $\mathsf{PoWMedianBlockSpan}$, are
+unchanged.
+
+## Non-consensus changes
+
+From NU8 activation:
+
+- Wallets SHOULD use a default expiry delta of 300 blocks, in place of the 120
+  blocks recommended by ZIP 218.
+- Nodes SHOULD support rolling back at least 1,500 blocks, in place of the 600
+  blocks recommended by ZIP 218.
+- Implementations SHOULD multiply the block-count constants that ZIP 218
+  multiplies by 3 by $\mathsf{NU8PoWTargetSpacingRatio}$, rounding up.
+- Nodes SHOULD NOT admit to their mempools or relay, and wallets SHOULD NOT
+  create, a transaction that alone exceeds the block size or shielded action
+  limits above.
+
+
+# Rationale
+
+A target spacing of 10 seconds makes each scaled quantity an integer: the
+averaging window of 255 blocks, the halving interval of 12,600,000 blocks, the
+address period of 262,500 blocks, and the limits of 800,000 bytes, 132
+actions, and 120 Sapling inputs and outputs.
+
+Every post-NU7 halving height is even on both networks. An even activation
+height $B$ therefore maps each such height $H$ to the integer height
+$B + 5(H - B)/2$, so that no halving boundary falls within a 25-second block.
+
+Scaling the per-block limits by 2/5 keeps the worst-case validation work,
+compact sync bandwidth, and chain growth per unit of time at their NU7 values.
+ZIP 218 bounds worst-case compact sync bandwidth at 169.10 MB per day.
+[^zip-0218] Without the scaling, each of these would increase by a factor of
+5/2.
+
+The post-NU8 block subsidy differs from 2/5 of the post-NU7 block subsidy by
+less than one zatoshi, due to rounding. If NU8 activates before the third
+halving, this reduces total scheduled issuance, relative to ZIP 218, by
+$(H_3 - B)/2$ zatoshi before the third halving and by 1.134 ZEC after it.
+
+
+# Security and Privacy Considerations
+
+The stale block rate increases with the ratio of block propagation time to the
+block target spacing. ZIP 218 reports a stale block rate of 4.86% for 2 MB
+blocks at 25-second spacing on a 99-node devnet. [^zip-0218] The rate at
+10-second spacing has not been measured; it needs to be measured before
+deployment. Smaller blocks and compact block relay [^draft-compact-block-relay]
+reduce propagation time.
+
+A given number of confirmations corresponds to 2.5 times less time. Where
+propagation time is significant relative to the target spacing, it also
+provides less security against an attacker with a given fraction of the hash
+power.
+
+Wallets that select an anchor three blocks behind the chain tip, as
+recommended by ZIP 315 [^zip-0315], select one about 30 seconds old. A rollback
+past the anchor invalidates the transaction, and links its revealed nullifiers
+to any later transaction that spends the same notes. More frequent blocks also
+give observers finer timing information.
+
+
+# Deployment
+
+This proposal is intended to be deployed in NU8. The NU8 deployment ZIP will
+specify $\mathsf{NU8ActivationHeight}$ for each network.
+
+
+# References
+
+[^BCP14]: [Information on BCP 14 — "RFC 2119: Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels" and "RFC 8174: Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words"](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp14)
+
+[^protocol]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, Version 2026.8.0 or later](protocol/protocol.pdf)
+
+[^protocol-networks]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, Version 2026.8.0. Section 3.12: Mainnet and Testnet](protocol/protocol.pdf#networks)
+
+[^protocol-constants]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, Version 2026.8.0. Section 5.3: Constants](protocol/protocol.pdf#constants)
+
+[^protocol-blockheader]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, Version 2026.8.0. Section 7.6: Block Header Encoding and Consensus](protocol/protocol.pdf#blockheader)
+
+[^protocol-diffadjustment]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, Version 2026.8.0. Section 7.7.3: Difficulty adjustment](protocol/protocol.pdf#diffadjustment)
+
+[^zip-0200]: [ZIP 200: Network Upgrade Mechanism](zip-0200.rst)
+
+[^zip-0207]: [ZIP 207: Funding Streams](zip-0207.rst)
+
+[^zip-0214]: [ZIP 214: Consensus rules for a Zcash Development Fund](zip-0214.rst)
+
+[^zip-0218]: [ZIP 218: 25-second Block Target Spacing](zip-0218.md)
+
+[^zip-0237]: [ZIP 237: Network Sustainability Mechanism: Halving-Preserving Issuance](zip-0237.md)
+
+[^zip-0259]: [ZIP 259: Deployment of the NU7 Network Upgrade](zip-0259.md)
+
+[^zip-0315]: [ZIP 315: Best Practices for Wallet Implementations](zip-0315.rst)
+
+[^draft-compact-block-relay]: [Draft ZIP: Compact Block Relay](https://github.com/zcash/zips/pull/1429)

+By “applink” we mean a platform mechanism for triggering local applications

+The terms below are to be interpreted as follows:
+
+URI-Encapsulated Payment (or *liberated payment*)
+  An amount of ZEC that is held by a *payment wallet* whose sole spending
+  secret is carried inside a URI, so that whoever holds the URI can take the
+  funds. "Liberated payment" is a product-neutral synonym used in user-facing
+  contexts; the two terms are interchangeable in this document.
+Payment-Encapsulating URI (or *payment URI*)
+  The URI that carries a URI-Encapsulated Payment, as specified in `Syntax`_.
+Payment secret
+  The 32-byte secret $S$ carried in the ``key`` parameter of a payment URI,
+  from which every key of the payment wallet is derived.
+Payment wallet
+  The single-account wallet derived from a payment secret as specified in
+  `Payment wallet derivation`_.
+Payment address
+  The Orchard-protocol payment address of the payment wallet to which the funds
+  of a URI-Encapsulated Payment are sent: in the *Orchard pool* before NU6.3
+  activation, and in the *Ironwood pool* from NU6.3 activation onward.
+Minter
+  The party (and their wallet software) that creates a payment URI and funds
+  its payment address. This is the *sender* of the payment.
+Claimant
+  The party (and their wallet software) that uses a payment URI to move the
+  funds held by the payment wallet into a wallet of their own. In the usual
+  case this is the intended *recipient* of the payment.
+Funding transaction
+  A transaction that sends funds to the payment address.
+Claim transaction
+  A transaction, created by a claimant, that spends all of the spendable notes
+  held by a payment wallet to one of the claimant's own addresses.
+Reclaim
+  A claim transaction created by the minter, taking back funds that were not
+  claimed by anyone else.
 
 
 Abstract
 ========
 
-This proposal specifies a mechanism for sending Zcash payments via any unmodified (secure) messaging service, e.g., Signal or WhatsApp. The sender need not know the recipient's address and the recipient need not have a Zcash wallet already installed. Payments occur via an ordinary text/WhatsApp/Signal message containing a URI. The URI encodes the secret spending key of an ephemeral Zcash “wallet address”, to which the funds have been transferred. Anyone who learns the URI can accept this payment, by a “finalization” process which uses the key given in the URI to transfer the encapsulated funds to their own wallet. After the payment is finalized, via a suitable on-chain transaction by the recipient, it becomes irrevocable.
-
-The proposal specifies the syntax and semantics of URI-Encapsulated Payments, the workflow of generating and handling them, and requisite infrastructure.
-
-At its core, a URI encapsulated payment communicates the existence of a transaction (specifically a note committing to an amount of funds) to a receiving client.  The URI encodes the amount of the payment and a key used to derive all necessary randomness for note construction including the address and secret key needed to spend it.
+This proposal specifies a mechanism for sending Zcash payments via any
+unmodified (secure) messaging service, printed medium, or other channel over
+which a short string can be conveyed. The sender need not know the recipient's
+address and the recipient need not have a Zcash wallet already installed.
+
+A payment is created by deriving a fresh 32-byte *payment secret*, deriving a
+*payment wallet* from that secret, and sending funds to its payment address,
+an Orchard-protocol address (funded in the Ironwood pool from NU6.3
+activation onward). The payment secret, together with a block height from which
+the funds can be found and optional advisory metadata (amount and description),
+is encoded in the fragment of an ordinary HTTPS URL. Because the fragment is
+never sent to the server named by the URL, the host serves only as an applink_
+target for wallet software and as a landing page for recipients without a
+compatible wallet.
+
+Anyone who learns the URI can claim the payment: their wallet derives the
+payment wallet, scans the chain from the given height, and sweeps every note it
+finds into an address of its own in a single transaction, taking the whole
+balance rather than the advertised amount. Until that happens the minter can
+take the funds back by the same procedure; there is no on-chain expiry and no
+limit on the age of a payment. A claim transaction is normally an ordinary
+fully-shielded transaction,
+indistinguishable on chain from any other, and it is constructed so that the
+payment secret does not grant visibility of where the funds went after the
+claim.
+
+The proposal specifies the syntax and semantics of Payment-Encapsulating URIs,
+the derivation of payment wallets, the workflow of minting, claiming and
+reclaiming payments, and the behaviour expected of wallet software and of
+hosts that appear in payment URIs. It also describes, informatively, the
+payment-link formats already deployed by the Vizor wallet, which follow the
+same model of a bearer secret for a standard single-account wallet.
 
 Usage Story
 -----------
 
-Alice wants to send a 1.23 ZEC payment to Bob. She doesn't have Bob's Zcash address — and Bob may not even have a wallet or have heard of Zcash! However, she does have some end-to-end encrypted channel to Bob on a secure messaging app, such as Signal or WhatsApp. She instructs her own Zcash wallet to send 1.23 ZEC on that channel. Her wallet then automatically generates a new ephemeral Zcash address and sends 1.23001 ZEC to this address. It then constructs a payment URI containing the secret key corresponding to the ephemeral address, and sends it to Bob via the secure messaging app.
+Alice wants to send a 1.23 ZEC payment to Bob. She doesn't have Bob's Zcash
+address — and Bob may not even have a wallet or have heard of Zcash! However,
+she does have some end-to-end encrypted channel to Bob on a secure messaging
+app, such as Signal or WhatsApp. She instructs her own Zcash wallet to send
+1.23 ZEC on that channel. Her wallet derives a new payment secret from her
+wallet seed, sends 1.2301 ZEC to the corresponding payment address, and
+constructs a payment URI containing the payment secret, which she sends to Bob
+via the secure messaging app.
 
 Bob receives the message, which looks as follows:
 
     This message contains a Zcash payment.
-    Click the following link to view it and receive the funds using your Zcash wallet app:
+    Click the following link to view it and receive the funds using your Zcash
+    wallet app:
 
-    https://pay.withzcash.com:65536/v1#amount=1.23&desc=Payment+for+foo&key=...
+    https://example.com/#v=1&key=zgift1...&height=3400000&amount=1.23&desc=Payment%20for%20foo
 
     If you do not yet have a Zcash wallet app, see: https://z.cash/wallets
 
-Bob clicks the link. His Zcash mobile wallet app (which is already installed and has configured itself as a handler for URLs of that form) shows up, and tells Bob that a payment of 1.23 ZEC awaits him. The wallet app confirms the existence of the pertinent transactions on the blockchain, and then offers to finalize the payment. Bob clicks the “Finalize” button, and his wallet app generates a transaction moving the money to his own address (using the extra 0.00001 ZEC he has received to pay the transaction fee). When this transaction is confirmed on-chain, Alice's and Bob's wallets both indicate that the payment is finalized, and thus Bob can send the funds to other parties.
-
-
-Motivation
-==========
+Bob clicks the link. His Zcash mobile wallet app (which is already installed
+and has configured itself as an applink_ handler for ``example.com``) shows up
+and tells Bob that a payment of about 1.23 ZEC awaits him. The wallet app
+scans the block chain from block 3400000 for the funds, confirms that they are
+present and unspent, and offers to claim the payment. Bob clicks the “Claim”
+button, and his wallet app generates a transaction moving the money to his own
+address (using the extra 0.0001 ZEC he has received to pay the transaction
+fee). When this transaction is confirmed on chain the payment is final, and
+Bob can send the funds to other parties.
 
-This proposal enables sending of funds without exposing users to the notion of payment addresses and their secure distribution. Instead, funds can be sent using any pre-existing communication channel, by a single message sent unidirectionally from the sender to the recipient. This message conveys all the information needed to obtain control of the funds, compactly expressed as a textual URI.
+If Bob had no compatible wallet installed, following the link would instead
+have shown him a static web page at ``example.com`` explaining what the link
+is and where to get a wallet; the page never learns the payment secret, which
+stays in the fragment on Bob's device.
 
-Consequently, all functionality related to contact discovery and secure-channel establishment can be delegated to the message app(s) with which the user is already familiar, and in which the user has already established communication channels to many of their contacts.
+The same mechanism serves "gift card" style uses: a merchant or event
+organiser mints a batch of payments, prints each URI as a QR code, and funds
+each card once. Whoever receives a card claims it; cards that are never
+claimed are reclaimed by the minter after an announced date.
 
-Moreover, funds can be sent to users who have not yet installed wallet software and who do not yet have a payment address. The recipient can collect the funds at any later time by installing suitable software.
 
-Additionally, the proposal greatly improves the scalability of Zcash. If a recipient only receives URI payments, they need not scan the blockchain or delegate their view keys to a third party to do so.
+Motivation
+==========
 
-Finally, this avoids the fat-finger problem of sending funds to the wrong address. The user sends funds via a known contact on, e.g., WhatsApp, who they have a relationship with or at least can confirm the recipient's identity. Moreover, even once funds are sent via a URI, they can be recovered if the other party does not claim them.
+This proposal enables sending of funds without exposing users to the notion of
+payment addresses and their secure distribution. Instead, funds can be sent
+using any pre-existing communication channel, by a single message sent
+unidirectionally from the sender to the recipient. This message conveys all
+the information needed to obtain control of the funds, compactly expressed as
+a textual URI.
+
+Consequently, all functionality related to contact discovery and secure-channel
+establishment can be delegated to the message app(s) with which the user is
+already familiar, and in which the user has already established communication
+channels to many of their contacts.
+
+Moreover, funds can be sent to users who have not yet installed wallet software
+and who do not yet have a payment address. The recipient can collect the funds
+at any later time by installing suitable software. This also makes the
+mechanism suitable for onboarding: a payment URI can be printed, handed out at
+an event, or embedded in a gift card, and the recipient's first interaction
+with Zcash can be receiving money rather than generating an address.
+
+Finally, this avoids the fat-finger problem of sending funds to the wrong
+address. The user sends funds via a known contact on, e.g., WhatsApp, who they
+have a relationship with or at least can confirm the recipient's identity.
+Moreover, even once funds are sent via a URI, they can be recovered if the
+other party does not claim them.
+
+The proposal is complementary to ZIP 321 [#zip-0321]_, which standardizes
+*Payment Request URIs* with which the payment *recipient* conveys their
+persistent payment address to the *sender*, for subsequent fund transfers (to
+be done using the normal on-chain mechanism rather than the encapsulated
+payments described in the current proposal).
+
+
+Privacy Implications
+====================
 
-The proposal is complementary to ZIP 321 [#zip-0321]_, which will standardize *Payment Request URIs* using which the payment *recipient* can convey their persistent payment address to the *sender*, for subsequent fund transfers (to be done using the normal on-chain mechanism rather than the encapsulated payments described in the current proposal).
+A URI-Encapsulated Payment involves two on-chain transactions: a funding
+transaction from the minter to the payment address, and a claim transaction
+from the payment address to the claimant. Both are normally fully-shielded
+transactions and are not distinguishable on chain from other transactions in
+the same pool, except through timing correlation and the statistics of their
+numbers of actions.
+
+The holder of a payment URI holds the payment wallet's full viewing key. They
+can therefore see the funding transaction(s) and the fact that the notes were
+spent. The claim transaction is specified so that its output is *not*
+decryptable with the payment wallet's outgoing viewing key; consequently a
+party who later obtains the URI (for example, from a chat backup or a
+discarded printed card) learns that the payment was claimed, but not the
+claimant's address or any other details of the claim output. The trade-off is
+that the claimant's own wallet is the only record of where the funds went.
+
+The minter learns when (and that) a payment was claimed, because the notes it
+can view become spent. The ``amount`` and ``desc`` parameters are readable by
+anyone who sees the URI, including in retrospect.
+
+The host named in a payment URI never receives the payment secret in an HTTP
+request, because it is carried in the fragment. However, any script served by
+that host *can* read the fragment, so the host operator (or anyone who can
+modify its content) is in a position to steal unclaimed funds if the landing
+page is not static. Wallet software that handles the URI through an applink_
+avoids any request to the host at all.
 
 
 Requirements
 ============
 
-This proposal's specification of URI-Encapsulated Payments, and the intended protocols for using them, is meant to fulfill the following requirements:
+This proposal's specification of URI-Encapsulated Payments, and the intended
+protocols for using them, is meant to fulfill the following requirements:
+
+* The protocol must not require the sender of a payment to stay online until
+  the recipient receives the URI (let alone claims the payment).
 
-* The protocol must not require the sender of a payment to stay online until the recipient receives the URI (let alone finalizes the payment).
+* URIs should be short enough to render conveniently, to fit in a QR code of
+  modest size, and to be compatible with length-limited messaging platforms.
 
-* For convenient rendering, URIs should be short; this also maximizes compatibility with length-limited messaging platforms.
+* It must not be feasible for someone who has not seen the URI (or has
+  compromised a party who has) to collect the funds.
 
-* It must not be feasible for someone who has not seen the URI (or has compromised a party who has) to collect the funds.
+* No server, indexer, or other third party should need to learn the payment
+  secret, and claiming should be possible using only the ordinary light-client
+  infrastructure that a shielded wallet already depends on.
 
-* The URIs and protocol should minimize the likelihood of inadvertent misuse, and in particular the risks discussed in “Security Considerations” below.
+* The URIs and protocol should minimize the likelihood of inadvertent misuse,
+  and in particular the risks discussed in `Security Considerations`_ below.
 
-* The protocol must not leak any information (sender identity, recipient identity, amount, description) to third parties, other than inevitable metadata about the existence of a transaction, the inevitable network communication around sending/receipt of transactions, whatever leakage is induced by the communication channel used to transmit the URI, and whatever is voluntarily shared by the parties.
+* The protocol must not leak any information (sender identity, recipient
+  identity, amount, description) to third parties, other than inevitable
+  metadata about the existence of a transaction, the inevitable network
+  communication around sending/receipt of transactions, whatever leakage is
+  induced by the communication channel used to transmit the URI, and whatever
+  is voluntarily shared by the parties.
 
-* The URIs should allow for future modifications and expansion of the format, without risk of ambiguous parsing.
+* The URIs should allow for future modifications and expansion of the format,
+  without risk of ambiguous parsing.
 
-* The on-chain footprint of payments that use this mechanism should be indistinguishable from normal fully-shielded transactions (except, possibly, for the statistics of the number of shielded inputs and outputs).
+* The on-chain footprint of payments that use this mechanism should be
+  indistinguishable from normal fully-shielded transactions (except, possibly,
+  for the statistics of the number of shielded inputs and outputs).
 
-* Don't lose funds, even if wallets crash, or everything but the sending wallet master secret is lost.
+* A payment should remain claimable for as long as its funds are unspent, so
+  that a payment that is printed, kept, or opened late does not silently
+  become unclaimable.
+
+* Don't lose funds, even if wallets crash, or everything but the sending
+  wallet master secret is lost. Payments minted by a wallet should be
+  recoverable from that wallet's seed, and a payment URI on its own should be
+  recoverable by any wallet that can restore a standard mnemonic phrase.
 
 Non-requirements
 ================
 
-* It is outside the scope of this proposal to establish a secure communication channel for transmission of URI-Encapsulated Payments, or to protect the parties' devices from security compromise.
+* It is outside the scope of this proposal to establish a secure communication
+  channel for transmission of URI-Encapsulated Payments, or to protect the
+  parties' devices from security compromise.
+
+* Claiming the payment may involve significant wait times, on the scale of
+  minutes, as the requisite on-chain transactions are generated, mined and
+  confirmed, and as the claimant's wallet scans the chain from the given
+  height. This proposal does not try to solve this (though it does try to
+  avoid imposing significant additional delays, and it does address how the
+  intermediate state is conveyed to the user).
+
+* A URI-Encapsulated Payment is not a long-term store of value and is not a
+  substitute for a wallet backup. See `Security Considerations`_.
 
-* Finalizing the payment may involve significant wait times, on the scale of minutes, as the requisite on-chain transactions are generated, mined and confirmed. This proposal does not try to solve this (though it does try to avoid imposing significant additional delays, and it does address how the intermediate state is conveyed to the user).
+* This proposal does not provide an on-chain expiry for unclaimed payments.
+  Reclaiming is a wallet-side action of the minter.
 
 
 Specification
 =============
 
-A Payment-Encapsulating URI represents the capability to claim the Zcash funds from specific on-chain transactions, as long as they're unspent. See `Usage Story`_ for an example.
+A Payment-Encapsulating URI represents the capability to claim whatever
+spendable funds are held, now or later, by the payment wallet derived from the
+payment secret it carries. See `Usage Story`_ for an example.
 
 Syntax
 ------
 
-A Payment-Encapsulating URI is a Universal Resource Locator (URL), as defined in RFC 3986 [#RFC3986]_, of the following form.
-
-Scheme: ``https``
-
-Host: ``pay.withzcash.com``
-
-Port: ``65536`` (this is intentionally not a valid TCP/IP port number)
-
-Path: ``payment/v1``
-
-Fragment parameters: these attribute-value pairs, in this order, separated by ``&``, and with all values percent-encoded where necessary:
-
-* ``amount=...`` where the attribute is a decimal number representing the amount of ZEC included in the payment. MUST be present.
-  If a decimal fraction is present then a period (.) MUST be used as the separating character to separate the whole number from the decimal fraction, and both the whole number and the decimal fraction MUST be nonempty. No other separators (such as commas for grouping or thousands) are permitted. Leading zeros in the whole number or trailing zeros in the decimal fraction are ignored. There MUST NOT be more than 8 digits in the decimal fraction.
-* ``desc=...`` where the attribute is a human-readable string associated with the payment. MAY be present.
-  If present, it MUST be encoded as “textual data consisting of characters from the Universal Character Set” as specified in RFC 3986 section 2.5.
-* ``key=`` is a 256-bit random number encoded with Bech32 as specified in Section 5.6.9 of the Zcash Protocol Specification [#protocol]_). MUST be present.
-
+A Payment-Encapsulating URI is a Uniform Resource Locator (URL), as defined in
+RFC 3986 [#RFC3986]_, with the following structure::
+
+  payment-uri  = "https://" host [ ":" port ] path-abempty "#" fragment
+  fragment     = param *( "&" param )
+  param        = version / keyparam / heightparam / amountparam / descparam
+               / otherparam
+  version      = "v=1"
+  keyparam     = "key=" bech32m
+  heightparam  = "height=" %x31-39 *DIGIT
+  amountparam  = "amount=" 1*DIGIT [ "." 1*8DIGIT ]
+  descparam    = "desc=" *qchar
+  otherparam   = 1*( ALPHA / DIGIT / "-" / "_" ) "=" *qchar
+  qchar        = unreserved / pct-encoded / "+"
+
+where ``host``, ``port``, ``path-abempty``, ``unreserved``, ``pct-encoded``,
+``ALPHA``, and ``DIGIT`` are as defined in RFC 3986 [#RFC3986]_, and
+``bech32m`` is a Bech32m string as specified in `Encoding of the payment
+secret`_. This grammar describes the URIs that producers emit; the handling of
+other input by consumers is specified below.
+
+The scheme MUST be ``https``; consumers MUST match it case-insensitively, as
+RFC 3986 requires. The ``host`` MAY be any host; see `Hosts and landing
+pages`_. The path SHOULD be empty or ``/``. Producers MUST NOT include a query
+component (``?``): everything specific to the payment MUST be carried in the
+fragment, so that it is never sent to the host. Consumers MUST NOT use a query
+component, if one is present, to interpret the payment.
+
+The fragment consists of attribute-value pairs separated by ``&``. The
+following attributes are defined:
+
+* ``v``: the format version. MUST be present and MUST have the value ``1`` for
+  URIs conforming to this version of this specification. A consumer that
+  encounters any other value MUST reject the URI as unsupported.
+* ``key``: the payment secret, encoded as specified in `Encoding of the
+  payment secret`_. MUST be present.
+* ``height``: a block height, in decimal without sign, whitespace or leading
+  zeros, at or before the height of the first funding transaction, and no less
+  than the minimum birthday height given in `Semantics`_. MUST be present.
+* ``amount``: the nominal amount of the payment in decimal ZEC, following the
+  same syntax and interpretation as the ``amount`` parameter of ZIP 321
+  [#zip-0321-amount]_; in addition, it MUST be greater than zero. MAY be
+  present. This value is advisory; see `Semantics`_.
+* ``desc``: a human-readable description of the payment. MAY be present. The
+  value is UTF-8 text [#RFC3629]_, percent-encoded as described below, and
+  MUST NOT exceed 512 bytes after decoding.
+
+The attributes ``v``, ``key`` and ``height`` are *strict*, and ``amount`` and
+``desc`` are *advisory*.
+
+Producers MUST emit ``v`` first, followed by ``key``, ``height``, ``amount``
+(if present) and ``desc`` (if present), in that order. Consumers MUST accept
+the defined attributes in any order.
+
+Consumers process the fragment as follows:
+
+* Empty pairs (as produced by ``&&``, or by a leading or trailing ``&``) MUST
+  be skipped.
+* A pair that contains no ``=`` is read as a name with an empty value.
+* Pairs whose name is not a defined attribute MUST be ignored, whether or not
+  they contain ``=``, so that future versions of this specification can add
+  optional attributes without changing ``v``.
+* Consumers MUST reject a URI in which a strict attribute is absent, appears
+  more than once, or is malformed or out of range.
+* If an advisory attribute appears more than once, or its value is malformed
+  or out of range (for ``amount``: not of the syntax above, zero, or greater
+  than the maximum money supply; for ``desc``: not decodable as described
+  below, or longer than 512 bytes after decoding), consumers MUST treat that
+  attribute as absent and MUST NOT reject the URI for that reason.
+
+Producers MUST percent-encode every byte of the ``desc`` value other than the
+``unreserved`` characters of RFC 3986 (``ALPHA``, ``DIGIT``, ``-``, ``.``,
+``_``, ``~``); in particular a space MUST be encoded as ``%20``. Consumers
+MUST decode ``%XX`` sequences and MUST treat an unencoded ``+`` as a space (for
+compatibility with form-encoding libraries). A ``desc`` value that contains a
+``%`` not followed by two hexadecimal digits, or that does not decode to valid
+UTF-8, is malformed.
+
+A Payment-Encapsulating URI MUST NOT exceed 16384 bytes. Consumers MAY reject
+longer inputs, measured after removing leading and trailing whitespace, before
+parsing them.
+
+Rationale for advisory attributes being lenient
+'''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''
+
+.. raw:: html
+
+   <details>
+   <summary>Click to show/hide</summary>
+
+The funds held by the payment wallet are authoritative, and ``amount`` and
+``desc`` only describe them. Rejecting a URI because one of them is malformed
+would make a funded payment unclaimable in conforming wallets because of a
+display-only field, which is the worse failure for a bearer instrument that
+may already be printed. The strict attributes, by contrast, determine which
+wallet is scanned and from where; guessing at them could hide funds or point
+the claimant at the wrong wallet.
+
+.. raw:: html
+
+   </details>
+
+Sanitization of the description
+'''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''
+
+The ``desc`` value is text chosen by whoever produced the URI. Before
+displaying it, or using it in any other way (for example in a memo), a
+consumer MUST transform the decoded value as follows:
+
+* each line break, paragraph separator or other whitespace control character
+  (TAB, LF, VT, FF, CR, NEL U+0085, LINE SEPARATOR U+2028 and PARAGRAPH
+  SEPARATOR U+2029) is replaced by a space;
+* every other control character (Unicode general category ``Cc``, that is the
+  C0 controls, DEL and the C1 controls) is removed;
+* the invisible format characters that can hide or reorder displayed text are
+  removed: the bidirectional marks (U+061C, U+200E, U+200F), the bidirectional
+  embeddings, overrides and isolates (U+202A to U+202E and U+2066 to U+2069),
+  the deprecated format controls (U+206A to U+206F), ZERO WIDTH SPACE
+  (U+200B), WORD JOINER and the invisible operators (U+2060 to U+2064), ZERO
+  WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE (U+FEFF), and the interlinear annotation controls
+  (U+FFF9 to U+FFFB).
+
+ZERO WIDTH JOINER, ZERO WIDTH NON-JOINER and variation selectors are kept,
+since emoji sequences and several scripts depend on them. If the result is
+empty or consists only of whitespace, ``desc`` is treated as absent.
+
+Producers MUST NOT emit a ``desc`` value that is blank, or that this
+transformation would change.

+The ``key`` parameter deterministically determines a payment wallet, as
+specified in `Payment wallet derivation`_. The URI represents the capability to
+spend all funds received by that wallet, in any pool.
+
+The ``height`` parameter is the *birthday* of the payment wallet: the block
+height from which a consumer scans the chain for the payment wallet's notes.
+It MUST be less than or equal to the height of the block containing the first
+funding transaction for the payment address. A producer SHOULD set it as close
+to that height as it can determine at the time the URI is generated (for
+example, the chain tip height when the funding transaction is created), since
+a smaller value only increases the claimant's scanning cost. A consumer MUST
+NOT assume that no notes exist below ``height``; it simply does not look for
+them.
+
+``height`` MUST be greater than or equal to the *minimum birthday height* of
+the network identified by ``key``: the activation height of NU5, which is
+1687104 on Mainnet and 1842420 on Testnet, or 1 on Regtest. Consumers MUST
+reject a URI whose ``height`` is lower. A payment wallet's Orchard funds
+cannot predate the activation of NU5, which introduced the Orchard pool.
+There is no upper bound and no lower bound relative to the chain tip; see
+`Payment Rendering and Blockchain Lookup`_.
+
+The ``amount`` and ``desc`` parameters are advisory. They exist so that wallet
+software can describe the payment to the user before the chain has been
+scanned. The amount that can actually be claimed is the total value of the
+unspent notes held by the payment wallet, less the transaction fee
+of the claim transaction, and MAY differ from ``amount`` in either direction
+(possibly being zero).
+
+The recipient's wallet software SHOULD convey to the user that the ``amount``
+and ``desc`` values are merely claims made by the party who sent the URI, and
+may be tentative, inaccurate or malicious.
+
+In particular, the recipient's wallet software SHOULD convey to the user that
+the amount of ZEC they can successfully transfer to their wallet may be
+different than that given by the ``amount`` parameter, and may change
+(possibly to zero), until the claim transaction has been mined.
+
+The payment associated with a URI is not deemed “received” by the recipient
+until a claim transaction has been mined; see `Claiming`_.

+Encoding of the payment secret
+------------------------------
+
+The payment secret $S$ is a sequence of exactly 32 bytes. It is encoded in the
+``key`` parameter using Bech32m [#bip-0350]_, with the 32 bytes converted to
+5-bit groups as for a Bech32 data part [#zip-0173]_ and with the following
+Human-Readable Parts:
+
+============== =====================
+Network        Human-Readable Part
+============== =====================
+Mainnet        ``zgift``
+Testnet        ``zgifttest``
+Regtest        ``zgiftregtest``
+============== =====================
+
+A Bech32m-encoded payment secret is 52 data characters plus the 6-character
+checksum, the ``1`` separator, and the Human-Readable Part.
+
+Producers MUST use lowercase. Consumers MUST accept either all-lowercase or
+all-uppercase encodings (so the Human-Readable Part is matched
+case-insensitively), as for Bech32, and MUST reject:
+
+* a string whose checksum is not a valid *Bech32m* checksum (in particular a
+  string carrying a Bech32 checksum MUST be rejected);
+* a string whose decoded data part is not exactly 32 bytes;
+* a string whose padding bits (the 4 bits left over when the 52 5-bit groups
+  are converted to 32 bytes) are not all zero, since these would give a second
+  spelling of the same secret;
+* a string that mixes lowercase and uppercase characters;
+* a string whose Human-Readable Part is not one of those listed above
+  ("unsupported network");
+* a string whose Human-Readable Part identifies a network other than the one
+  the consuming wallet is operating on ("wrong network"). A wallet MUST NOT
+  derive or display a payment address for a payment secret on the wrong
+  network, and SHOULD tell the user which network the URI is for.
+
+.. note::
+    The Human-Readable Parts above are specific to this ZIP. If a registry of
+    Bech32/Bech32m Human-Readable Parts used by Zcash is established (for
+    example in ZIP 173 [#zip-0173]_ or ZIP 316 [#zip-0316]_), the entries
+    ``zgift``, ``zgifttest`` and ``zgiftregtest`` are to be registered for
+    "ZIP 324 payment secret" on Mainnet, Testnet and Regtest respectively.
+
+Payment wallet derivation
+-------------------------
+
+Given a payment secret $S$ and a network, the payment wallet is derived as
+follows:
+
+1. Let $\mathsf{mnemonic}$ be the BIP 39 [#bip-0039]_ mnemonic sentence
+   obtained from the 256 bits of entropy $S$ using the English word list. This
+   is a 24-word sentence whose final 8 bits are the BIP 39 checksum of $S$.
+2. Let $\mathsf{seed}$ be the 64-byte BIP 39 seed derived from
+   $\mathsf{mnemonic}$ with an empty passphrase (that is, with the PBKDF2 salt
+   ``"mnemonic"``).
+3. Let $\mathit{coin\_type}$ be the SLIP 44 [#slip-0044]_ coin type for the
+   network: $133$ for Mainnet and $1$ for Testnet and Regtest.
+4. Let $\mathsf{sk}$ be the Orchard spending key at ZIP 32 path
+   $m_\mathsf{Orchard} / 32' / \mathit{coin\_type}' / 0'$ derived from
+   $\mathsf{seed}$ as specified in ZIP 32 [#zip-0032-orchard]_ (that is,
+   account $0$ of the seed).
+5. The *payment address* is the Orchard-protocol diversified payment address
+   of $\mathsf{sk}$ at diversifier index $0$
+   [#protocol-orchardkeycomponents]_. When the payment address needs to be
+   encoded, it MUST be encoded as a Unified Address [#zip-0316]_ containing
+   only that Orchard Receiver. An Orchard-protocol receiver is scoped to the
+   Orchard protocol rather than to a pool, so the same receiver accepts funds
+   in the *Orchard pool* and in the *Ironwood pool* [#zip-0326-receiving]_.
+   If NU6.3 introduces a distinct encoding for Ironwood-pool payments, that
+   encoding is to be used as specified by ZIP 258 [#zip-0258]_ and the ZIPs it
+   cites; see `Open Questions`_.
+
+The Orchard full viewing key, incoming viewing key and outgoing viewing key of
+the payment wallet are those of $\mathsf{sk}$.
+
+The payment wallet is the whole of account $0$ of $\mathsf{seed}$: besides
+its Orchard keys, it has the Sapling keys at ZIP 32 path
+$m_\mathsf{Sapling} / 32' / \mathit{coin\_type}' / 0'$
+[#zip-0032-sapling]_, and the transparent keys of the BIP 44 [#bip-0044]_ account
+$0$ for $\mathit{coin\_type}$. Its Orchard-protocol keys serve both the
+*Orchard pool* and the *Ironwood pool*.
+
+A minter funds the payment address as follows:
+
+* for a funding transaction mined before NU6.3 activation, the minter SHOULD
+  fund the payment address in the *Orchard pool*;
+* from NU6.3 activation onward, value can no longer enter the *Orchard pool*
+  [#zip-0258-nu63-rules]_ and wallets do not send to external receivers in
+  it [#zip-0326-keygen]_, so the minter MUST fund the payment address in the
+  *Ironwood pool*.
+
+A minter SHOULD NOT send funds to a Sapling address of the payment wallet, and
+MUST NOT advertise a transparent receiver for it. Funds can nevertheless reach other
+addresses of the payment wallet, for example if someone pays one of its
+transparent addresses out of band, or if a deployed format advertised a
+Sapling receiver (see `Known Uses`_).
+
+A claimant MUST scan for the payment wallet's funds in every shielded pool
+(Orchard, Ironwood and Sapling) and at its transparent addresses, and MUST
+sweep all of them as specified in `Claiming`_. Spending from the *Orchard
+pool* remains possible after NU6.3 activation, so Orchard-pool funds of
+payments minted earlier stay claimable.
+
+Implementations MAY compute $\mathsf{seed}$ directly from $S$ without
+materialising the mnemonic sentence, provided the result is identical.
+
+Rationale for an Orchard-protocol payment address and an all-pool claim

+The Orchard protocol is used because it is the current shielded protocol,
+with the best privacy properties and the cheapest proofs on mobile devices,
+and because a Unified Address with a single Orchard Receiver keeps the payment
+address short. The funding pool follows the current pool for that protocol:
+the *Orchard pool* before NU6.3 activation and the *Ironwood pool* after it,
+when the consensus rules no longer let value enter the *Orchard pool*.
+Funding the current pool also keeps the usual claim transaction free of
+cross-pool transfers, which would be visible on chain as changes in pool
+balances.
+
+Sweeping everything the payment wallet holds costs the recipient no privacy:
+the payment wallet is single-use, its keys are already known to the minter
+and to every holder of the URI, the destination is a shielded receiver of the
+claimant, and the payment wallet's outgoing viewing key is not used. Leaving
+funds in a pool that the claimant does not scan would only strand them, or
+leave them for whichever other holder of the URI takes them. Some deployed
+payment links (see `Known Uses`_) describe a payment address with both
+Orchard and Sapling receivers, so Sapling funds do occur in practice.

+Deriving the ZIP 32 seed via a BIP 39 mnemonic rather than directly from $S$
+means that the payment wallet is an ordinary single-account wallet: any Zcash
+wallet that can restore a 24-word phrase can recover the funds of a payment
+URI, even if it has no support for this ZIP, by restoring the phrase and
+scanning from the birthday. This provides a recovery path independent of any
+particular software and lets a wallet "upgrade" a payment into a persistent
+wallet if it chooses. The cost is one PBKDF2 derivation of 2048 iterations,
+which is negligible.

+Minting a payment secret
+------------------------
 
+A payment secret MUST have 256 bits of entropy. It is obtained in one of two
+ways.
+
+**Seed-derived secrets.** A wallet that mints payments from a ZIP 32 seed $S_w$
+(the wallet's own seed, not to be confused with the payment secret) MUST derive
+payment secrets using ZIP 32 registered key derivation
+[#zip-0032-registered]_, with:
+
+- $\mathsf{ContextString} = \texttt{“Zcash\_URIEncapsulatedPayment”}$
+- $\mathsf{ZipNumber} = 324$
+
+The payment secret with index $\mathit{index}$ on the network with SLIP 44
+coin type $\mathit{coin\_type}$ is the 32-byte key component of
+
+$\mathsf{CKDreg}(\mathsf{CKDreg}(\mathsf{RegKD}(\texttt{“Zcash\_URIEncapsulatedPayment”}, S_w, 324), \mathit{coin\_type} + 2^{31}, [\,]), \mathit{index} + 2^{31}, [\,])$
+
+where the chain code of the resulting child is discarded. In path notation
+this is $m_{\texttt{Zcash\_URIEncapsulatedPayment}} / 324' / \mathit{coin\_type}' / \mathit{index}'$,
+where $m_{\texttt{Zcash\_URIEncapsulatedPayment}}$ is the master key that
+registered key derivation computes from the context string and $S_w$; the
+$324'$ step is the $\mathsf{ZipNumber}$ step that $\mathsf{RegKD}$ performs.
+ZIP 32 defines no general path notation for registered key derivation; this
+one is unambiguous because every step uses an empty tag.
+
+$\mathit{index}$ MUST be in the range $\{ 0\,..\, 2^{31} - 1 \}$. A minting
+wallet MUST NOT reuse an index for which it has previously produced a URI, and
+SHOULD allocate indices sequentially starting from $0$ so that payments can be
+recovered as described in `Recovery From Wallet Crash`_.
+
+**Random secrets.** A minter that does not derive payments from a seed (for
+example a service that mints payments in bulk) MAY instead generate $S$
+uniformly at random using a cryptographically secure random number generator.
+Such a minter is responsible for its own record of outstanding secrets if it
+intends to reclaim payments.

+Hosts and landing pages
+-----------------------
+
+The ``host`` of a Payment-Encapsulating URI serves two purposes: it is the
+domain against which wallet software registers an applink_ handler, and it
+serves a *landing page* to users whose device has no wallet that handles the
+URI.
+
+A wallet that supports this ZIP SHOULD register as an applink_ handler for the
+hosts whose payment URIs it intends to handle, and MUST also accept a payment
+URI pasted or shared into it directly, regardless of host, provided that the
+URI conforms to `Syntax`_.
+
+The operator of a host that appears in payment URIs:
+
+* MUST serve the association files required by the applink_ mechanisms of the
+  platforms it supports, listing the wallet applications that may handle its
+  URIs, and SHOULD publish the policy under which applications are listed;
+* MUST NOT serve, at the path used by payment URIs, any script or other
+  active content that reads the fragment identifier, transmits it, or
+  stores it — including analytics, error-reporting and tag-management
+  scripts;
+* SHOULD serve a static page that explains that the link carries a Zcash
+  payment, that the funds can be taken by anyone who has the link, and how to
+  obtain a compatible wallet;
+* SHOULD serve the page with HTTP headers that prevent the fragment from
+  leaking through referrers (for example a ``Referrer-Policy`` of
+  ``no-referrer``) and that restrict script execution (for example a
+  ``Content-Security-Policy`` without ``script-src``).
+
+A wallet that opens a payment URI through an applink_ does not contact the
+host at all. A wallet MUST NOT fetch the URI over the network itself.

+Minting and funding
+-------------------
+
+The minter's wallet:
+
+1. Obtains a payment secret $S$ as specified in `Minting a payment secret`_,
+   and derives the payment address as specified in `Payment wallet
+   derivation`_.
+2. Chooses ``height``, which MUST be at most the height at which the funding
+   transaction is mined. A wallet that generates the URI before the funding
+   transaction is mined SHOULD use the chain tip height at the time the
+   funding transaction is created.
+3. Durably records the payment, as described below, before broadcasting any
+   funding transaction.
+4. Creates and broadcasts a *funding transaction* paying the payment address.
+   The funding output is an output to the payment address in the pool
+   required by `Payment wallet derivation`_: the *Orchard pool* (SHOULD)
+   before NU6.3 activation, and the *Ironwood pool* (MUST) from NU6.3
+   activation onward. The funding transaction SHOULD be a
+   fully-shielded transaction, so that it is indistinguishable from ordinary
+   transactions, and MAY carry ``desc`` (or nothing) in the memo of the
+   funding output.
+5. Encodes the payment URI as specified in `Syntax`_.
+
+The funding amount SHOULD include, in addition to the nominal amount shown in
+``amount``, a *fee reserve* so that the claimant receives the nominal amount
+after paying the fee of the claim transaction. The RECOMMENDED reserve is
+10000 zatoshis, which is the ZIP 317 [#zip-0317]_ conventional fee of a claim
+transaction with at most two logical actions. A minter that funds the same
+payment address with more than one note SHOULD increase the reserve by 5000
+zatoshis for each additional note beyond the second, since each additional
+spend adds a logical action.
+
+The minter's wallet MUST NOT expose the payment address as a receiving address
+of the minter, and SHOULD NOT send the same payment address more than one
+funding transaction, except to top up a payment before the URI has been
+transmitted.
+
+Before broadcasting the funding transaction, the minter's wallet MUST durably
+record enough information to find and reclaim the payment: for a seed-derived
+secret, its index and ``height``; for a random secret, the secret itself and
+``height``. This ensures that a crash between broadcast and recording cannot
+leave funds in a payment wallet that no one knows about. The minter's wallet
+SHOULD also record the nominal amount and ``desc``, so that it can display
+status and reclaim the payment without rescanning. The minter's wallet MUST
+retain the ability to derive the payment wallet of every payment it has
+minted (see `Recovery From Wallet Crash`_).
+
+A minter whose spending keys are held by a hardware signer creates the
+funding transaction through its usual signing flow (for example using a
+Partially Created Zcash Transaction [#zip-0374]_). Hardware custody protects
+only the funding account: the payment secret and the payment wallet's keys
+always exist on the host device, and later on the claimant's device.
+Seed-derived payment secrets require the wallet seed, so a minter whose seed
+is available only to a hardware signer uses random secrets (see `Minting a
+payment secret`_) or a seed that is available to the host.
+
+Clients MAY generate and transmit the URI before the funding transaction is
+mined; the claimant's wallet will show the payment as *Pending* until it is.

+Intake of payment URIs
+----------------------
+
+Payment URIs may reach a wallet from any web page or application that can
+trigger an applink_, so a wallet MUST bound the resources that incoming URIs
+can consume:
 
+* it MUST apply the length limit of `Syntax`_ before any other processing;
+* it SHOULD bound the number of payment URIs awaiting processing at any one
+  time, and SHOULD treat a URI that designates the same payment wallet as one
+  already awaiting processing as a duplicate rather than processing it twice;
+* a malformed URI MUST NOT prevent the processing of other URIs; and
+* it MUST NOT begin scanning for, or claiming, a payment solely because a URI
+  was received (see `Claiming`_).

+This ZIP sets no confirmation numbers of its own; the classification of
+funds as trusted or untrusted is what matters, and ZIP 315 supplies the
+policy. It has been argued that a single confirmation suffices for the
+funding notes, because they were created expressly for a single-use wallet and
+so the usual concerns about untrusted senders do not apply. Provenance is not
+the risk, however: the minter still holds the payment secret (and, for
+seed-derived secrets, can always re-derive it), as may other parties who have
+seen the URI. If a chain reorganization removes the funding transaction or
+the claim transaction, the minter can double-spend the funding transaction's
+inputs, or another holder of the URI can have their own claim mined instead,
+and the claimant's apparent receipt disappears. These are exactly the risks
+that the ZIP 315 policy for untrusted TXOs addresses. The claim transaction
+itself is different: it is created on the claimant's device, so its output is
+trusted (see `Claiming`_).
